title.en: Volume 92 Biographies 42: Wei Yuanzhong, Wei Anshi, Ziao Zhizhong, Zong Chuke, Ji Chune

sentences.zh: 魏元忠韋安石

translations.literal: Wei Yuanzhong and Wei Anshi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong and Wei Anshi

sentences.zh: （子陟斌斌子況從父兄子抗從祖兄子巨源趙彥昭附）

translations.literal: (With appended biographies of his sons Zhi and Bin, Bin's son Kuang, his father's brother's son Kang, his grandfather's brother's son Juyuan, and Zhao Yanzhao)
translations.idiomatic: (With appended accounts of his sons Zhi and Bin, Bin's son Kuang, his paternal cousin Kang, his grand-uncle's grandson Juyuan, and Zhao Yanzhao)

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠

translations.literal: Xiao Zhizhong
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhizhong

sentences.zh: （宗楚客紀處訥附）

translations.literal: (With appended biographies of Zong Chuke and Ji Chune)
translations.idiomatic: (With appended accounts of Zong Chuke and Ji Chune)

sentences.zh: 魏元忠，宋州宋城人也。

translations.literal: Wei Yuanzhong was a native of Songcheng in Song prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong came from Songcheng in Song prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名真宰，以避則天母號改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Zhenzai; it was changed to avoid the taboo on Empress Wu's mother's title.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Zhenzai; he changed it to avoid the taboo on the posthumous title of Empress Wu's mother.

sentences.zh: 初，為太學生，志氣倜儻，不以舉薦為意，累年不調。

translations.literal: At first he was a student at the Imperial Academy, bold and free-spirited in temperament, and paid no heed to recommendation for office; for many years he received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he studied at the Imperial Academy, spirited and unconventional, and cared little about securing a recommendation; for years he went without an official post.

sentences.zh: 時有左史盩厔人江融撰《九州設險圖》，備載古今用兵成敗之事，元忠就傳其術。

translations.literal: At the time the Left Historiographer Jiang Rong of Zhouzhi compiled the Diagram of Strategic Terrain in the Nine Provinces, fully recording successes and failures in warfare ancient and modern; Yuanzhong went to him to learn the art.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Left Historiographer Jiang Rong of Zhouzhi wrote the Diagram of Strategic Terrain in the Nine Provinces, a comprehensive record of military successes and failures through history, and Yuanzhong studied the art under him.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，吐蕃頻犯塞，元忠赴洛陽上封事，言命將用兵之工拙，曰：

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era, when the Tibetans repeatedly raided the frontier, Yuanzhong went to Luoyang and submitted a sealed memorial on the skill and clumsiness of appointing generals and employing troops, saying:
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng reign, as Tibetans repeatedly breached the border, Yuanzhong traveled to Luoyang and submitted a sealed memorial on how well or poorly generals were chosen and armies deployed. He wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞理天下之柄，二事焉，文與武也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in governing All-under-Heaven there are two handles: civil and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that governing the realm rests on two pillars: civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 然則文武之道，雖有二門，至於製勝禦人，其歸一揆。

translations.literal: Thus although the ways of civil and military learning have two gates, in achieving victory and controlling others they converge on one standard.
translations.idiomatic: Though civil and military learning follow different paths, when it comes to prevailing over foes and mastering others, both aim at the same end.

sentences.zh: 方今王略遐宣，皇威遠振，建禮樂而陶士庶，訓軍旅而懾生靈。

translations.literal: At present the royal design is proclaimed afar and imperial majesty shakes the distance: rites and music are established to mold scholars and commoners, and armies are trained to awe the people.
translations.idiomatic: Today the royal design reaches far and imperial might resounds abroad: rites and music shape the educated and the common people, while disciplined armies keep all living under heaven in awe.

sentences.zh: 然論武者以弓馬為先，而不稽之以權略；

translations.literal: Yet those who discuss military affairs put bow and horse first and do not examine matters by strategy;
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who speak of war prize archery and horsemanship above all and never weigh matters by strategic calculation;

sentences.zh: 談文者以篇章為首，而不問之以經綸。

translations.literal: those who discuss letters put compositions first and do not inquire into statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: while those who speak of letters prize literary compositions and never ask whether a man can govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 而奔競相因，遂成浮俗。

translations.literal: Rivalry and scrambling follow one upon another, and so a shallow custom has formed.
translations.idiomatic: Rivalry feeds on rivalry until the age has sunk into empty fashion.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗讀魏、晉史，毎鄙何晏、王衍終日談空。

translations.literal: Your subject has read the histories of Wei and Jin and always despised how He Yan and Wang Yan spent whole days discoursing on emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: When I read the histories of Wei and Jin, I have always despised how He Yan and Wang Yan could spend entire days discoursing on emptiness.

sentences.zh: 近觀齊、梁書，才士亦復不少，並何益於理亂哉？

translations.literal: Reading recently the histories of Qi and Liang, talented men are likewise not few—yet what did any of them profit order and disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Looking recently at the histories of Qi and Liang, one finds no lack of talented men—yet what did any of them do for the rise or fall of states?

sentences.zh: 從此而言，則陸士衡著《辨亡論》，而不救河橋之敗，養由基射能穿劄，而不止鄢陵之奔，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: From this it may be said: Lu Shiheng wrote the Discourse on Perishing States yet could not save the defeat at Heqiao; Yang Youji's shooting could pierce a willow leaf yet could not halt the rout at Yanling—it can be known for certain.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows: Lu Ji wrote his Discourse on Perishing States yet could not avert defeat at Heqiao; Yang Youji's arrows could pierce a willow leaf yet could not stop the flight at Yanling—the lesson is plain.

sentences.zh: 昔趙岐撰禦寇之論，山濤陳用兵之本，皆坐運帷幄，暗合孫、吳。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhao Qi wrote a discourse on repelling invaders and Shan Tao set forth the foundations of employing troops; both sat directing from within the curtain and tacitly matched Sunzi and Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhao Qi wrote on repelling invaders and Shan Tao expounded the foundations of war; both directed campaigns from behind the curtain in ways that tacitly matched Sunzi and Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 宣尼稱“有德者必有言，仁者必有勇”，則何平叔、王夷甫豈得同日而言載！

translations.literal: Confucius said, "The virtuous must have words; the benevolent must have courage"—how then could He Pingshu and Wang Yifu be spoken of in the same breath!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "The virtuous must have words to speak; the benevolent must have courage"—how then could He Yan and Wang Yan ever be mentioned in the same breath!

sentences.zh: 臣聞才生於代，代實須才，何代而不生才，何才而不生代。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that talent is born from an age and an age truly needs talent—what age does not produce talent, what talent does not produce an age?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that talent arises from its age and every age truly needs talent—what age has ever lacked talent, what talent has ever lacked its age?

sentences.zh: 故物有不求，未有無物之歲；

translations.literal: Thus there are things not sought, but there has never been a year without things;
translations.idiomatic: There are things no one seeks, yet there has never been a year without goods to be had;

sentences.zh: 士有不用，未有無士之時。

translations.literal: there are gentlemen not employed, but there has never been a time without gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: there are scholars left unused, yet there has never been an age without men of talent.

sentences.zh: 夫有誌之士，在富貴之與貧賤，皆思立於功名，冀傳芳於竹帛。

translations.literal: Men of resolve, whether in wealth and honor or in poverty and low station, all think to establish merit and fame and hope to leave a fragrant name on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Men of resolve, whether rich or poor, high or low, all wish to win merit and fame and hope their names will live on in the histories.

sentences.zh: 故班超投筆而歎，祖逖擊楫而誓，此皆有其才而申其用矣。

translations.literal: Thus Ban Chao threw down his brush and sighed, and Zu Ti struck the oar and vowed—these all had their talent and brought their use to fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Chao threw down his brush and sighed; Zu Ti struck the oar and swore his oath—each had talent and found the chance to use it.

sentences.zh: 且知己難逢，英哲罕遇，士之懷琬琰以就埃塵，抱棟梁而困溝壑者，則悠悠之流，直睹此士之貧賤，安知此士之方略哉。

translations.literal: Moreover, a true knower is hard to meet and heroic sages are rarely encountered; when a gentleman bearing jade goes to dust and one embracing pillar-timbers is trapped in a ditch, the multitude only sees this gentleman's poverty and low station—how would they know this gentleman's strategy?
translations.idiomatic: Yet true patrons are rare and heroic rulers seldom appear; when a man carrying jade sinks into the dust and one who could be a pillar of state languishes in a ditch, the crowd sees only his poverty—how could they know his designs?

sentences.zh: 故漢拜韓信，舉軍驚笑；

translations.literal: Thus when Han enfeoffed Han Xin, the whole army was startled and laughed;
translations.idiomatic: When Han appointed Han Xin, the whole army was astonished and laughed;

sentences.zh: 蜀用魏延，群臣觖望。

translations.literal: when Shu employed Wei Yan, the ministers were discontent.
translations.idiomatic: when Shu employed Wei Yan, the ministers were resentful.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，富貴者易為善，貧賤者難為功，至於此也！

translations.literal: Alas! The rich and honored easily do good; the poor and lowly hardly achieve merit—such is the case!
translations.idiomatic: Alas! The rich and honored find it easy to do good, while the poor and lowly can scarcely achieve merit—so it has always been.

sentences.zh: 亦有位處立功之際，而不展其志略，身為時主所知，竟不能盡其才用，則貧賤之士焉足道哉！

translations.literal: There are also those who stand at the moment to establish merit yet do not display their designs; though known to the ruler of the age, in the end their talent is not fully used—how then can poor and lowly gentlemen be worth mentioning!
translations.idiomatic: Some men stand at the very moment to win glory yet never unfold their designs; though known to their sovereign, their gifts are never fully used—what wonder, then, that poor and obscure men go unheard?

sentences.zh: 漢文帝時，魏尚、李廣並身任邊將，位為郡守。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, Wei Shang and Li Guang both personally served as frontier generals, holding the rank of commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Han, Wei Shang and Li Guang both served on the frontier as commandery administrators.

sentences.zh: 文帝不知魏尚之賢而囚之，不知李廣之才而不能用之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen did not know Wei Shang's worth and imprisoned him; he did not know Li Guang's talent and could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen failed to recognize Wei Shang's worth and had him imprisoned; he failed to recognize Li Guang's talent and could not put him to use.

sentences.zh: 常歎李廣恨生不逢時，令當高祖日，萬戶侯豈足道哉。

translations.literal: He often sighed that Li Guang regretted being born out of season, saying that had he lived in the days of Emperor Gaozu, a marquisate of ten thousand households would scarcely be worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: He often lamented that Li Guang was born in the wrong age, saying that had he lived under Emperor Gaozu, a marquisate of ten thousand households would have been nothing to speak of.

sentences.zh: 夫以李廣才氣，天下無雙，匈奴畏之，號為“飛將”，爾時胡騎憑淩，足伸其用。

translations.literal: As for Li Guang's talent and spirit, none under heaven could match him; the Xiongnu feared him and called him the "Flying General"—at that time the barbarian horsemen pressed hard, enough to stretch his use to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang's talent and spirit were unmatched under heaven; the Xiongnu feared him and called him the Flying General—at a time when barbarian horsemen pressed the borders, he could have proved his full worth.

sentences.zh: 文帝不能大任，反歎其生不逢時。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen could not give him great employment, yet instead sighed that he was born out of season.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen would not give him great responsibility, yet sighed that he had been born in the wrong age.

sentences.zh: 近不知魏尚、李廣之賢，而乃遠想廉頗、李牧。

translations.literal: He did not know the worth of Wei Shang and Li Guang close at hand, yet looked far off to Lian Po and Li Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to recognize the worth of Wei Shang and Li Guang beside him, yet dreamed of Lian Po and Li Mu from ages past.

sentences.zh: 故馮唐曰，雖有頗、牧而不能用，近之矣。

translations.literal: Thus Feng Tang said: though one has Po and Mu, one cannot employ them—this is close to the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Feng Tang said: though one has men like Lian Po and Li Mu, one cannot use them—how near the truth that was.

sentences.zh: 從此言之，疏斥賈誼，復何怪哉。

translations.literal: From this it may be said: to cast out Jia Yi—what wonder is there in that?
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, is it any wonder that Jia Yi was cast aside?

sentences.zh: 此則身為時主所知，竟不能盡其才用。

translations.literal: This is the case of being known to the ruler of the age yet in the end not fully using one's talent.
translations.idiomatic: This is the case of a man known to his sovereign who is never allowed to use his gifts to the full.

sentences.zh: 晉羊祜獻計平吳，賈充、荀勖沮其策，祜歎曰：“天下不如意恒十居七八。”

translations.literal: In Jin, Yang Hu presented a plan to pacify Wu; Jia Chong and Xun Xu obstructed his strategy. Hu sighed and said: "Under heaven, things not as one wishes constantly occupy seven or eight parts in ten."
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Yang Hu proposed a plan to conquer Wu, but Jia Chong and Xun Xu blocked it. Hu sighed and said, "Under heaven, things go against one's wishes seven or eight times out of ten."

sentences.zh: 緣荀、賈不同，竟不大舉。

translations.literal: Because Xun and Jia disagreed, in the end no great campaign was launched.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xun and Jia disagreed, no great campaign was ever launched.

sentences.zh: 此則位處立功之際，而不得展其志略。

translations.literal: This is the case of standing at the moment to establish merit yet not being able to display one's designs.
translations.idiomatic: This is the case of a man placed at the moment to win glory who cannot unfold his designs.

sentences.zh: 而布衣韋帶之人，懷一奇，抱一策，上書闕下，朝進而望夕召，何可得哉。

translations.literal: As for men in plain cloth and leather belt who harbor one marvel and embrace one stratagem, submitting memorials below the palace gates and hoping to be summoned the same evening they arrive in the morning—how can that be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: As for commoners in plain dress who hold one brilliant plan and submit a memorial at court, hoping to be summoned the same evening they arrive—how can they expect such fortune?

sentences.zh: 臣請曆訪內外文武職事五品已上，得不有智計如羊祜、武藝如李廣，在用與不用之間，不得騁其才略。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to visit in turn all civil and military officials of fifth rank and above, inner and outer—may there not be some with strategy like Yang Hu or martial skill like Li Guang who, between employment and non-employment, cannot give rein to their talent and designs?
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we survey all civil and military officials of fifth rank and above, at court and in the provinces—are there not men with Yang Hu's strategic mind or Li Guang's martial prowess who, whether used or ignored, cannot fully deploy their gifts?

sentences.zh: 伏願降寬大之詔，使各言其誌。

translations.literal: Your subject bows and wishes that a broad and generous edict be issued, so that each may speak his intent.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty issue a broad and generous edict allowing every man to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 無令汲黯直氣，臥死於淮陽。

translations.literal: Do not let Ji An's upright spirit die abed in Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let a man of Ji An's upright spirit die in obscurity at Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 仲舒大才，位屈於諸侯相。

translations.literal: Zhongshu had great talent yet his rank was bent low as a feudal lord's chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu had great talent yet was reduced to serving as a feudal lord's chancellor.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞帝王之道，務崇經略。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the way of emperors and kings is to exalt grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the way of emperors and kings is to exalt grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 經略之術，必仗英奇。

translations.literal: The art of grand strategy must rely on extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Grand strategy depends on extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 自國家良將，可得言矣。

translations.literal: As for our state's fine generals, one may speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: Our own state's fine generals are proof enough.

sentences.zh: 李靖破突厥，侯君集滅高昌，蘇定方開西域，李勣平遼東，雖奉國威靈，亦其才力所致。

translations.literal: Li Jing broke the Turks, Hou Junji destroyed Gaochang, Su Dingfang opened the Western Regions, and Li Ji pacified Liaodong—though they followed the state's awesome might, it was also due to their own talent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing shattered the Turks, Hou Junji destroyed Gaochang, Su Dingfang opened the Western Regions, and Li Ji pacified Liaodong—though they served the state's majesty, their victories owed much to their own ability.

sentences.zh: 古語有之，“人無常俗，政有理亂，兵無強弱，將有能否”。

translations.literal: An old saying runs: "Men have no fixed customs; government has order and disorder; armies have no fixed strength or weakness—generals have ability or inability."
translations.idiomatic: An old saying has it: "Men have no fixed ways; governments rise and fall; armies are not inherently strong or weak—it is the general who makes the difference."

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，安邊境，立功名，在於良將也。

translations.literal: Viewed from this, to secure the borders and establish merit and fame lies in fine generals.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, securing the borders and winning glory depend on fine generals.

sentences.zh: 故趙充國征先零，馮子明討南羌，皆計不空施，機不虛發，則良將立功之驗也。

translations.literal: Thus Zhao Chongguo campaigned against the Xianling and Feng Ziming attacked the Southern Qiang—both plans were not applied in vain and opportunities were not launched to no purpose; this is proof of fine generals establishing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chongguo's campaign against the Xianling and Feng Ziming's attack on the Southern Qiang wasted neither plan nor opportunity—proof of what fine generals can achieve.

sentences.zh: 然兵革之用，王者大事，存亡所係。

translations.literal: Yet the use of arms is a great affair for a true king, on which survival and perishing depend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the use of arms is the gravest business of kings, on which survival itself depends.

sentences.zh: 若任得其才，則摧凶而扼暴。

translations.literal: If one appoints the right talent, one crushes the vicious and restrains the violent.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint the right man and you crush the vicious and restrain the violent.

sentences.zh: 苟非其任，則敗國而殄人。

translations.literal: If the appointment is wrong, one ruins the state and destroys the people.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint the wrong man and you ruin the state and destroy the people.

sentences.zh: 北齊段孝玄云：“持大兵者，如擎盤水。

translations.literal: Duan Xiaoxuan of Northern Qi said: "One who holds a great army is like one carrying a tray of water."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiaoxuan of Northern Qi said, "Commanding a great army is like carrying a tray of water."

sentences.zh: 傾在俯仰間，一致蹉跌，求止豈得哉！”

translations.literal: It spills in the space between bowing and looking up; one slip and how can one ask it to stop!
translations.idiomatic: It spills in an instant; one misstep and there is no stopping it!

sentences.zh: 從此而言，周亞夫堅壁以挫吳、楚，司馬懿閉營而困葛亮，俱為上策。

translations.literal: From this it may be said: Zhou Yafu held fast in his walls to break Wu and Chu, and Sima Yi closed camp to distress Zhuge Liang—both were supreme strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, Zhou Yafu's holding fast behind his walls to break Wu and Chu, and Sima Yi's closing camp to wear down Zhuge Liang, were both supreme strategies.

sentences.zh: 此皆不戰而卻敵，全軍以製勝。

translations.literal: These all repelled the enemy without fighting and preserved the whole army to achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: Each repelled the enemy without fighting and preserved the army intact to win.

sentences.zh: 是知大將臨戎，以智為本。

translations.literal: From this one knows that when a great general faces battle, intelligence is the root.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that when a great general faces battle, intelligence is the foundation.

sentences.zh: 漢高之英雄大度，尚曰“吾寧鬥智”；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han, heroic and magnanimous, still said, "I would rather contend in wits";
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han, heroic and magnanimous, still said, "I would rather match wits than strength";

sentences.zh: 魏武之綱神冠絕，猶依法孫、吳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei, whose commanding spirit crowned the age, still followed the laws of Sunzi and Wuzi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, whose commanding spirit crowned the age, still followed the teachings of Sunzi and Wuzi.

sentences.zh: 假有項籍之氣，袁紹之基，而皆泯智任情，終以破滅，何況復出其下哉！

translations.literal: Suppose one had Xiang Yu's spirit and Yuan Shao's foundation—yet both extinguished wisdom and followed emotion, and in the end were destroyed; how much more those below them!
translations.idiomatic: Men with Xiang Yu's spirit and Yuan Shao's foundation both abandoned strategy for impulse and were destroyed in the end—what hope for those beneath them?

sentences.zh: 且上智下愚，明暗異等，多算少謀，眾寡殊科。

translations.literal: Moreover, highest wisdom and lowest folly, brightness and darkness, differ in rank; many calculations and few plans, many and few, belong to different categories.
translations.idiomatic: The wise and the foolish, the clear-sighted and the blind, belong to different orders; the many calculations of the skilled and the few plans of the inept are worlds apart.

sentences.zh: 故魏用柏直以拒漢，韓信輕為豎子；

translations.literal: Thus when Wei employed Bo Zhi to resist Han, Han Xin despised him as a mere boy;
translations.idiomatic: When Wei employed Bo Zhi to resist Han, Han Xin dismissed him as a mere boy;

sentences.zh: 燕任慕容評以抗秦，王猛謂之奴才。

translations.literal: when Yan entrusted Murong Ping to resist Qin, Wang Meng called him a slave.
translations.idiomatic: when Yan entrusted Murong Ping to resist Qin, Wang Meng called him a lackey.

sentences.zh: 即柏直、慕容評智勇俱亡者也。

translations.literal: Bo Zhi and Murong Ping were men in whom wisdom and courage were both lost.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Zhi and Murong Ping were men utterly lacking in wisdom and courage.

sentences.zh: 夫中材之人，素無智略，一旦居元帥之任，而意氣軒昂，自謂當其鋒者無不摧碎，豈知戎昭果毅、敦《詩》說《禮》之事乎！

translations.literal: Men of middling talent, by nature without strategy, once placed in a marshal's post become lofty in spirit and deem that none who meet their edge can fail to be shattered—how would they know the affairs of martial clarity, resolute firmness, and earnest study of the Odes and exposition of the Rites!
translations.idiomatic: Men of middling talent, devoid of strategy, once made marshals swell with pride and believe nothing can withstand their charge—what do they know of martial discipline, resolute command, or the study of the Odes and Rites?

sentences.zh: 故李信求以二十萬眾獨舉鄢郢，其後果辱秦軍；

translations.literal: Thus Li Xin asked to take two hundred thousand men alone to raise Yan and Ying, and afterward indeed shamed Qin's army;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin asked to take two hundred thousand men alone against Yan and Ying, and in the end brought shame on Qin's army;

sentences.zh: 樊噲願得十萬眾橫行匈奴，登時見折季布，皆其事也。

translations.literal: Fan Kuai wished to take a hundred thousand men and sweep the Xiongnu, and was at once rebuffed by Ji Bu—these are all such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuai vowed to take a hundred thousand men and sweep the Xiongnu, only to be rebuffed at once by Ji Bu—such cases are legion.

sentences.zh: 當今朝廷用人，類取將門子弟，亦有死事之家而蒙抽擢者。

translations.literal: At present the court in employing men mostly takes sons of general families; there are also those from families of men who died in service who receive selection.
translations.idiomatic: Today the court mostly appoints sons of general families; some from families of men who died in service are also promoted.

sentences.zh: 此等本非幹略見知，雖竭力盡誠，亦不免於傾敗，若之何使當閫外之任哉？

translations.literal: Such men by nature are not known for capacity and strategy; though they exhaust effort and utmost loyalty, they cannot escape ruin—how can they be made to bear command beyond the passes?
translations.idiomatic: Such men are not known for ability or strategy; though they serve with utmost loyalty, they cannot escape defeat—how can they be entrusted with command beyond the frontier?

sentences.zh: 後漢馬賢討西羌，皇甫規陳其必敗；

translations.literal: In Later Han, Ma Xian campaigned against the Western Qiang and Huangfu Gui stated that he would certainly be defeated;
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, when Ma Xian campaigned against the Western Qiang, Huangfu Gui declared he would certainly fail;

sentences.zh: 宋文帝使王玄謨收復河南，沈慶之懸知不克。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song sent Wang Xuamo to recover Henan, and Shen Qingzhi knew in advance he could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Song sent Wang Xuamo to recover Henan, Shen Qingzhi knew beforehand he would fail.

sentences.zh: 謝玄以書生之姿，拒苻堅天下之眾，郗超明其必勝；

translations.literal: Xie Xuan in the bearing of a scholar repelled Fu Jian's hosts of all under heaven, and Chi Chao understood that he would certainly win;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan, a scholar in bearing, held off Fu Jian's hosts from across the realm, and Chi Chao foresaw his certain victory;

sentences.zh: 桓溫提數萬之兵，萬里而襲成都，劉真長期於決取。

translations.literal: Huan Wen led several tens of thousands of troops ten thousand li to strike Chengdu, and Liu Zhenchang expected a decisive capture.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen led tens of thousands of troops ten thousand li to strike Chengdu, and Liu Zhenchang expected a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 雖時有今古，人事皆可推之，取驗大體，觀其銳誌與識略耳。

translations.literal: Though times have past and present, human affairs may all be inferred; take proof from the broad pattern and observe keen resolve and strategic insight—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Though ages differ, human affairs follow the same patterns; judge the broad outcome by a man's keen resolve and strategic insight.

sentences.zh: 明者隋分而察，成敗之形，昭然自露。

translations.literal: The clear-sighted examine along the gradations, and the form of success and failure reveals itself plainly.
translations.idiomatic: The clear-sighted judge step by step, and the shape of victory or defeat reveals itself plainly.

sentences.zh: 京房有言，“後之視今，亦猶今之視古。”

translations.literal: Jing Fang had a saying: "Those later who view the present are just as those today who view antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang said, "Those who come after will view our age just as we view antiquity."

sentences.zh: 則昔賢之與今哲，意況何殊。

translations.literal: Then how different in intent and circumstance are sages of old and wise men of today?
translations.idiomatic: How different in spirit, then, are the sages of old from the wise men of today?

sentences.zh: 當事機之際也。

translations.literal: It is the moment when affairs hang in the balance.
translations.idiomatic: It is the moment when affairs hang in the balance.

sentences.zh: 皆隨時而立功，豈復取賢於往代，待才於未來也？

translations.literal: All establish merit according to the time—why again seek worthies from past ages or await talent from the future?
translations.idiomatic: Men win glory in their own age—why seek worthies only from the past or wait for talent from the future?

sentences.zh: 即論知與不知，用與不用。

translations.literal: This is to discuss knowing and not knowing, employing and not employing.
translations.idiomatic: This comes down to knowing talent or not, and using it or not.

sentences.zh: 夫建功者，言其所濟，不言所起；

translations.literal: In establishing merit one speaks of what one achieved, not of one's origins;
translations.idiomatic: When judging merit, speak of what a man accomplished, not where he came from;

sentences.zh: 言其所能，不言所藉。

translations.literal: one speaks of what one can do, not of what one relied on.
translations.idiomatic: speak of what he can do, not what connections he had.

sentences.zh: 若陳湯、呂蒙、馬隆、孟觀，並出自貧賤，勳濟甚高，未聞其家代為將帥。

translations.literal: Chen Tang, Lü Meng, Ma Long, and Meng Guan all came forth from poverty and low station; their merit and achievement were very high, and one has not heard that their families for generations were generals and marshals.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang, Lü Meng, Ma Long, and Meng Guan all rose from poverty and obscurity to win great merit, yet none came from a family of generals.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒曰：“為政之用，譬之琴瑟，不調甚者，必解弦而更張之，乃可鼓也。”

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu said: "The use of governing is like a zither or lute; when badly out of tune one must loosen the strings and stretch them anew before it can be played."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu said, "Governing is like a lute: when badly out of tune, one must loosen the strings and stretch them anew before it can be played."

sentences.zh: 故陰陽不和，擢士為相；

translations.literal: Thus when yin and yang are not in harmony, a scholar is raised to be chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang fall out of harmony, a scholar is raised to be chancellor;

sentences.zh: 蠻夷不龔，拔卒為將，即更張之義也。

translations.literal: when barbarians are not submissive, a common soldier is pulled up to be general—this is the meaning of stretching the strings anew.
translations.idiomatic: when barbarians grow rebellious, a common soldier is promoted to general—that is what it means to stretch the strings anew.

sentences.zh: 以四海之廣，億兆之眾，其中豈無卓越奇絕之士？

translations.literal: With the four seas so vast and the hundred millions so many, among them how could there not be outstanding and matchless gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: With the four seas so vast and hundreds of millions of people, how could there not be outstanding and matchless men among them?

sentences.zh: 臣恐未之思也，夫何遠之有。

translations.literal: Your subject fears they have not been thought of—how could they be far away?
translations.idiomatic: I fear only that Your Majesty has not thought to seek them—how could such men be far away?

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞賞者禮之基，罰者刑之本。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that reward is the foundation of rites and punishment is the root of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that reward is the foundation of rites and punishment the root of penal law.

sentences.zh: 故禮崇謀夫竭其能，賞厚義士輕其死，刑正君子勖其心，罰重小人懲其過。

translations.literal: Thus when rites exalt strategists, they exhaust their ability; when rewards are thick, men of righteousness lightly regard death; when penal law is correct, gentlemen are encouraged in heart; when punishments are heavy, petty men are chastised for their faults.
translations.idiomatic: When rites honor strategists, they give their all; when rewards are generous, men of honor face death lightly; when penal law is just, gentlemen are encouraged; when punishments are severe, the base are chastened for their faults.

sentences.zh: 然則賞罰者，軍國之綱紀，政教之藥石。

translations.literal: Thus reward and punishment are the cords and nets of army and state, the medicine and stone of government and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Reward and punishment are the cords that bind army and state, the medicine of government and instruction.

sentences.zh: 綱紀舉而眾務自理，藥石行而文武用命。

translations.literal: When the cords are raised, the myriad affairs govern themselves; when medicine and stone are applied, civil and military obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Raise those cords and the myriad affairs govern themselves; apply that medicine and civil and military alike obey.

sentences.zh: 彼吐蕃蟻結蜂聚，本非敵，薛仁貴、郭待封受閫外之寄，奉命專征，不能激勵熊羆，乘機掃撲。

translations.literal: Those Tibetans swarm like ants and bees—not true foes by nature—yet Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng received trust beyond the passes, were ordered on exclusive campaigns, and could not rouse the bear and brown nor seize the moment to sweep and strike them down.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans swarm like ants and bees and are no true match—yet Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng, entrusted with command beyond the passes and ordered on independent campaigns, could not rouse their troops or seize the moment to sweep them away.

sentences.zh: 敗軍之後，又不能轉禍為福，因事立功，遂乃棄甲喪師，脫身而走。

translations.literal: After the defeat they could not turn misfortune to fortune or achieve merit through events, and so they cast off armor, lost their army, and fled to save themselves.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat they could not turn disaster to triumph or win merit from the crisis; they cast off their armor, lost their army, and fled.

sentences.zh: 幸逢寬政，罪止削除，國家綱漏吞舟，何以過此。

translations.literal: By good fortune they met with lenient policy and their punishment stopped at dismissal; the state's net has holes large enough to swallow a boat—what surpasses this?
translations.idiomatic: By fortune they met lenient treatment and were merely dismissed; the state's laws are so lax they might as well have holes big enough to swallow a boat—what could exceed this?

sentences.zh: 天皇遲念舊恩，收其後效，當今朝廷所少，豈此一二人乎？

translations.literal: The Heavenly Sovereign has long borne in mind old kindness and awaits their later merit—what the court lacks today, is it only one or two such men?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor still remembers past service and awaits their future merit—is the court today really so short of capable men that it needs these two alone?

sentences.zh: 且賞不勸謂之止善，罰不懲謂之縱惡。

translations.literal: Moreover, when reward does not encourage, it is called stopping goodness; when punishment does not chastise, it is called indulging evil.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards fail to encourage, goodness ceases; when punishments fail to chastise, evil runs unchecked.

sentences.zh: 仁貴自宣力海東，功無尺寸，坐玩金帛，瀆貨無厭，今又不誅，縱惡更甚。

translations.literal: Rengui himself exerted strength in the eastern sea but his merit had no measure; he toyed with gold and silk and was insatiable in corrupt gifts—if he is not punished now, indulging evil will grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui exerted himself in the eastern sea campaign yet won no real merit; he hoarded gold and silk and was insatiable in bribes—if he goes unpunished now, indulgence of evil will only grow worse.

sentences.zh: 臣以疏賤，幹非其事，豈欲間天皇之君臣，生厚薄於仁貴？

translations.literal: Your subject, low and base, has interfered in what is not his affair—does he wish to come between the Heavenly Sovereign and his ministers, or breed ill will toward Rengui?
translations.idiomatic: I am lowly and presumptuous to speak on matters not my own—do I wish to come between Emperor and ministers, or breed ill will toward Rengui?

sentences.zh: 直以刑賞一虧，百年不復，區區所懷，實在於此。

translations.literal: It is simply that once reward and punishment are bent, they will not be restored for a hundred years; the humble concern your subject holds lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that once reward and punishment are bent, a century may pass before they are restored—and that is what weighs on my mind.

sentences.zh: 古人云：“國無賞罰，雖堯、舜不能為化。”

translations.literal: The ancients said: "In a state without reward and punishment, even Yao and Shun cannot bring transformation."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "In a state without reward and punishment, even Yao and Shun cannot bring transformation."

sentences.zh: 今罰不能行，賞亦難信，故人間議者皆言，“近日征行，虛有賞格而無其事。”

translations.literal: Today punishment cannot be carried out and reward is hard to believe, so people everywhere say, "Recent campaigns have empty reward scales with no fulfillment."
translations.idiomatic: Today punishment cannot be enforced and rewards are not believed, so people everywhere say, "Recent campaigns promise rewards that are never paid."

sentences.zh: 良由中才之人不識大體，恐賞賜勳庸，傾竭倉庫，留意錐刀，將此益國。

translations.literal: Truly it is because men of middling talent do not grasp the broad pattern, fearing that rewarding meritorious service would drain the treasury; they fix their minds on pennies, thinking thereby to benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: This is because men of middling talent fail to grasp the larger design, fearing that rewarding merit would drain the treasury; they fixate on pennies, thinking that will benefit the state.

sentences.zh: 徇目前之近利，忘經久之遠圖，所謂錯之毫厘，失之千里者也。

translations.literal: They pursue immediate near profit and forget far-reaching long-term plans—this is what is called missing by a hair's breadth and erring by a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: They pursue immediate profit and forget long-term design—missing by a hair's breadth, erring by a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 且黔首雖微，不可欺以得誌，瞻望恩澤，必因事而生心。

translations.literal: Moreover, though the common people are slight, one cannot deceive them about gaining their intent; gazing toward grace and favor, they will surely take events as cause to form designs in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Though the common people are humble, they cannot be deceived about what they hope for; watching for imperial favor, they will surely act on what they see.

sentences.zh: 既有所因，須應之以實，豈得懸不信之令，設虛賞之科？

translations.literal: Once there is cause, there must be response in fact—how can one suspend unbelievable orders and set empty reward statutes?
translations.idiomatic: Once they see cause, they expect real response—how can the throne issue unbelievable orders and set empty reward statutes?

sentences.zh: 比者師出無功，未必不由於此。

translations.literal: Recently armies have gone forth without merit—perhaps this is not unrelated to the above.
translations.idiomatic: Recent campaigns have failed to win merit—perhaps for no other reason than this.

sentences.zh: 文子曰：“同言而信，信在言前；

translations.literal: Wenzi said: "When words are alike, trust lies before the words;
translations.idiomatic: Master Wen said, "When words are alike, trust lies before the words;"

sentences.zh: 同令而行，誠在令外。”

translations.literal: when orders are alike, sincerity lies outside the order."
translations.idiomatic: when orders are alike, sincerity lies outside the order.

sentences.zh: 故商君移木以表信，曹公割發以明法，豈禮也哉，有由然也。

translations.literal: Thus Lord Shang moved a tree to display trust, and Duke Cao cut his hair to clarify law—was it ritual? There was reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shang moved a tree to display trust, and Cao Cao cut his hair to clarify the law—this was not mere ritual, but had its reason.

sentences.zh: 自蘇定方定遼東，李勣破平壤，賞絕不行，勳仍淹滯，數年紛紜，真偽相雜，縱加沙汰，未至澄清。

translations.literal: Since Su Dingfang pacified Liaodong and Li Ji broke Pingrang, rewards have ceased to be given and merit still stagnates; for years there has been confusion, true and false mixed, and though sifted, clarity has not been reached.
translations.idiomatic: Since Su Dingfang pacified Liaodong and Li Ji took Pyongyang, rewards have gone unpaid and merit has stagnated; for years confusion has reigned, true and false mixed, and though sifted, clarity has not been reached.

sentences.zh: 臣以吏不奉法，慢自京師，偽勳所由，主司之過。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that officials do not uphold the law, negligently from the capital; false merit arises from the fault of the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that officials do not uphold the law, starting negligently from the capital; false merit arises from the fault of the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 其則不遠，近在尚書省中，不聞斬一台郎，戮一令史，使天下知聞，天皇何能照遠而不照近哉！

translations.literal: The precedent is not far—it lies within the Ministry of Personnel; one hears of no desk officer beheaded, no clerk executed, to make all under heaven know: how can the Heavenly Sovereign illuminate the far and not the near!
translations.idiomatic: The precedent is close at hand—in the Ministry of Personnel itself; not one desk officer beheaded, not one clerk executed, to make the realm take notice: how can the Emperor see far and not near!

sentences.zh: 神州化首，萬國共尊，文昌政本，四方是則，軌物宣風，理亂攸在。

translations.literal: The divine land is the head of transformation, all states honor it together; the Secretariat is the root of government, the four quarters take it as model—setting standards and proclaiming wind, order and disorder depend on it.
translations.idiomatic: The divine land is the head of civilization, honored by all states; the Secretariat is the root of government, the model for the four quarters—setting standards and proclaiming policy, order and disorder depend on it.

sentences.zh: 臣是以披露不已，冒死盡言。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore discloses without end, risking death to speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I disclose without end, risking death to speak fully.

sentences.zh: 且明鏡所以照形，往事所以知今，臣識不稽古，請以近事言之。

translations.literal: Moreover, a bright mirror illuminates form and past affairs inform the present; your subject's knowledge does not examine antiquity—please allow him to speak from recent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A bright mirror shows form and past affairs inform the present; I do not claim knowledge of antiquity—let me speak from recent affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞觀年中，萬年縣尉司馬玄景舞文飾智，以邀乾沒，太宗審其奸詐，棄之都市。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Wannian county assistant Sima Xuanjing perverted texts to display cleverness and sought illicit profit; Taizong examined his treachery and abandoned him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, Wannian county assistant Sima Xuanjing twisted the law for profit; Taizong judged his treachery and had him executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 及征高麗也，總管張君乂擊賊不進，斬之旗下。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Goguryeo, overall commander Zhang Junyi attacked the bandits without advancing and was beheaded beneath his banner.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Goguryeo, overall commander Zhang Junyi failed to advance against the enemy and was beheaded beneath his banner.

sentences.zh: 臣以偽勳之罪，多於玄景；

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the crimes of false merit are more numerous than Xuanjing's;
translations.idiomatic: The crimes of false merit outnumber Xuanjing's;

sentences.zh: 仁貴等敗，重於君乂。

translations.literal: the defeats of Rengui and others are heavier than Junyi's.
translations.idiomatic: the defeats of Rengui and others outweigh Junyi's.

sentences.zh: 向使早誅薛仁貴、郭待封，則自餘諸將，豈敢失利於後哉？

translations.literal: Had Rengui and Guo Daifeng been punished early, would the other generals have dared to fail afterward?
translations.idiomatic: Had Rengui and Guo Daifeng been punished early, would the other generals have dared to fail afterward?

sentences.zh: 韓子云：“慈父多敗子，嚴家無格虜。”

translations.literal: Han Feizi said: "A fond father has many failed sons; a strict household has no unruly slaves."
translations.idiomatic: Han Feizi said, "A fond father has many failed sons; a strict household has no unruly slaves."

sentences.zh: 此言雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: Though this saying is small, it may illustrate what is large.
translations.idiomatic: Though this saying is small, it illustrates what is large.

sentences.zh: 公孫弘有言：“人主病不廣大，人臣病不節儉。”

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong had a saying: "The ruler's illness is not being broad and great; the minister's illness is not being frugal."
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong said, "The ruler's fault is lack of breadth; the minister's fault is lack of frugality."

sentences.zh: 臣恐天皇病之於不廣大，過在於慈父，斯亦日月之一蝕也。

translations.literal: Your subject fears the Heavenly Sovereign's illness lies in not being broad and great, the fault in being a fond father—this too is an eclipse of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the Emperor's fault lies in lack of breadth, in being too fond a father—this too is an eclipse of sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 又今之將吏，率多貪暴，所務唯狗馬，所求唯財物，無趙奢、吳起散金養士之風，縱使行軍，悉是此屬。

translations.literal: Moreover today's generals and officials are mostly greedy and violent; what they pursue is only dogs and horses, what they seek is only wealth—there is none of Zhao She or Wu Qi's style of scattering gold to nurture soldiers; even when marching, all are of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Today's generals and officials are mostly greedy and violent; they pursue horses and hounds and seek only wealth—none has Zhao She's or Wu Qi's spirit of spending gold to nurture troops; on campaign they are all alike.

sentences.zh: 臣恐吐蕃之平，未可旦夕望也。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that pacifying the Tibetans cannot be expected at dawn or dusk.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that pacifying the Tibetans cannot be expected soon.

sentences.zh: 帝甚歎異之，授秘書省正字，令直中書省，仗內供奉。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly marveled at him and appointed him Rectifier in the Secretariat, ordered to attend at the Secretariat, and attendant within the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly impressed and appointed him Rectifier in the Secretariat, with attendance at court and service in the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 尋除監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made supervisory censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made supervisory censor.

sentences.zh: 文明年，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Wenhua era he was promoted to palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wenhua era he was promoted to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 其年，徐敬業據揚州作亂，左玉鈐衛大將軍李孝逸督軍討之，則天詔元忠監其軍事。

translations.literal: That year Xu Jingye held Yangzhou in rebellion; Left Jade Bell Guard General Li Xiaoyi commanded the army to attack him, and Zetian ordered Yuanzhong to oversee the military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xu Jingye seized Yangzhou in rebellion; Left Jade Bell Guard General Li Xiaoyi commanded the army against him, and Empress Wu ordered Yuanzhong to oversee military affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝逸至臨淮，而偏將雷仁智為敬業先鋒所敗，敬業又攻陷潤州，回兵以拒孝逸。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi reached Linhuai, and the flank general Lei Renzhi was defeated by Jingye's vanguard; Jingye also captured Runzhou and turned his army to resist Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi reached Linhuai, where flank general Lei Renzhi was defeated by Jingye's vanguard; Jingye also captured Runzhou and turned to face Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 孝逸懼其鋒，按甲不敢進。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi feared his edge and held his armor without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi feared Jingye's momentum and held his army without advancing.

sentences.zh: 元忠謂孝逸曰：“朝廷以公王室懿親，故委以閫外之事，天下安危，實資一決。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said to Xiaoyi: "The court, because you are a close kinsman of the imperial house, has entrusted you with affairs beyond the passes; the safety of all under heaven truly depends on one decision from you.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said to Xiaoyi, "The court has entrusted you with command beyond the passes because you are imperial kin; the safety of the realm depends on your single decision.

sentences.zh: 且海內承平日久，忽聞狂狡，莫不注心傾耳，以俟其誅。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the seas there has long been peace; suddenly hearing of this mad rebel, none fail to fix their hearts and incline their ears, awaiting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has long been at peace; at news of this rebel, all await his destruction.

sentences.zh: 今大軍留而不進，則解遠近之望，萬一朝廷更命他將代公，其將何辭以逃逗撓之罪？

translations.literal: If the great army now stays without advancing, it will disappoint hopes near and far; should the court appoint another general to replace you, with what words will he escape the crime of delay and hesitation?
translations.idiomatic: If the army now holds back, it will disappoint hopes near and far; should the court replace you with another general, how will he escape the charge of delay?

sentences.zh: 幸速進兵以立大效，不然，則禍難至矣。”

translations.literal: I pray you advance the army quickly to establish great merit; otherwise calamity will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Advance quickly and win great merit; otherwise disaster will come.

sentences.zh: 孝逸然其言，乃部勒士卒以圖進討。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi approved his words and thereupon arrayed his troops to plan attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi agreed and arrayed his troops for attack.

sentences.zh: 時敬業屯於下阿溪，敬業弟敬猷率偏師以逼淮陰。

translations.literal: At that time Jingye was encamped at Xia'a Creek, and Jingye's younger brother Jingyou led a flank force to press Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye was encamped at Xia'a Creek, and his younger brother Jingyou led a flank force against Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 元忠請先擊敬猷，諸將咸曰：“不如先攻敬業，敬業敗，則敬猷不戰而擒矣。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong asked to strike Jingyou first; the generals all said: "Better first attack Jingye—when Jingye is defeated, Jingyou will be taken without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong asked to strike Jingyou first; the generals all said, "Better attack Jingye first—once Jingye falls, Jingyou will be taken without a fight."

sentences.zh: 若擊敬猷，則敬業引兵救之，是腹背受敵也。”

translations.literal: If we attack Jingyou, Jingye will lead troops to rescue him, and we will be attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: If we attack Jingyou, Jingye will come to his rescue and we will be caught between two armies.

sentences.zh: 元忠曰：“不然，賊之勁兵精卒，盡在下阿，蟻聚而來，利在一決，萬一失捷，則大事雲矣。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said: "Not so. The rebels' crack troops and picked soldiers are all at Xia'a, swarming like ants with victory hanging on one battle—if we should fail, great affairs will be lost in clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said, "No. The rebels' best troops are all at Xia'a, massed for a decisive battle—one defeat and all is lost.

sentences.zh: 敬猷本出博徒，不習戰鬥，其眾寡弱，人情易搖，大軍臨之，其勢必克。

translations.literal: Jingyou by nature came from gamblers and is unskilled in battle; his host is few and weak, men's hearts easily shaken—when the great army presses him, he is sure to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyou is a gambler by origin, unskilled in war; his force is small and weak, morale easily shaken—the great army will surely defeat him.

sentences.zh: 既克敬猷，我之乘勝而進。

translations.literal: Once Jingyou is taken, we advance in victory.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingyou is defeated, we advance in victory.

sentences.zh: 彼若引救淮陰，計程則不及，又恐我之進掩江都，必邀我於中路。

translations.literal: If he leads troops to rescue Huaiyin, by reckoning the route he cannot arrive in time; he will also fear we advance to cover Jiangdu and must intercept us midway.
translations.idiomatic: If he marches to rescue Huaiyin, he cannot arrive in time; he will also fear we advance on Jiangdu and must intercept us on the road.

sentences.zh: 彼則勞倦，我則以逸待之，破之必矣。

translations.literal: He will be weary and we will await him at ease—defeating him is certain.
translations.idiomatic: He will be weary while we wait at ease—defeat is certain.

sentences.zh: 譬之逐獸，弱者先擒，豈可舍必擒之弱獸，趨難敵之強兵？

translations.literal: It is like chasing beasts: seize the weak first—how can one abandon a beast sure to be taken and rush at hard-to-fight strong troops?
translations.idiomatic: It is like hunting: take the weak first—how abandon prey sure to fall and rush at the strong?

sentences.zh: 恐未可也。”

translations.literal: I fear it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That cannot be right.

sentences.zh: 孝逸從之，乃引兵擊敬猷，一戰而破之，敬猷脫身而遁。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi followed this, led troops to attack Jingyou, and broke him in one battle; Jingyou escaped in person.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi agreed, attacked Jingyou, and routed him in one battle; Jingyou fled.

sentences.zh: 孝逸乃進軍，與敬業隔溪相拒。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi then advanced his army and faced Jingye across the creek.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi then advanced and faced Jingye across the creek.

sentences.zh: 前軍總管蘇孝祥為賊所破，孝逸又懼，欲引退。

translations.literal: Front-army overall commander Su Xiaoxiang was broken by the bandits; Xiaoyi again grew afraid and wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Front-army commander Su Xiaoxiang was defeated; Xiaoyi again grew afraid and wished to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 初，敬業至下阿，有流星墜其宮，及是，有群烏飛噪於陣上，元忠曰：“驗此，即賊敗之兆也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jingye reached Xia'a, a meteor fell on his camp; now flocks of crows flew crying over the battle lines. Yuanzhong said: "Verified by this, it is the omen of the bandits' defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingye reached Xia'a, a meteor had fallen on his camp; now crows cried over the lines. Yuanzhong said, "This proves the rebels will be defeated.

sentences.zh: 風順荻乾，火攻之利。”

translations.literal: The wind favors us and the reeds are dry—the advantage lies in fire attack."
translations.idiomatic: The wind favors us and the reeds are dry—fire attack will prevail."

sentences.zh: 固請決戰，乃平敬業。

translations.literal: He firmly asked for decisive battle and thereupon pacified Jingye.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed for battle and pacified Jingye.

sentences.zh: 元忠以功擢司刑正，稍遷洛陽令。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice for his merit and soon moved up to magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Justice for his merit and soon became magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 尋陷周興獄，詣市將刑，則天以元忠有討平敬業功，特免死配流貴州。

translations.literal: Soon he fell into Zhou Xing's prison, was taken to the market to be executed; Zetian, because Yuanzhong had the merit of pacifying Jingye, specially spared his death and sentenced him to exile in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell into Zhou Xing's prison and was taken to the execution ground; Empress Wu, remembering his merit in pacifying Jingye, spared his life and exiled him to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 時承敕者將至市，先令傳呼，監刑者遽釋元忠令起，元忠曰：“未知敕虛實，豈可造次。”

translations.literal: When the bearer of the edict was about to reach the market, he was first ordered to call out; the overseer of execution hastily released Yuanzhong and told him to rise. Yuanzhong said: "Not knowing whether the edict is real or false, how can one act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict-bearer was about to reach the market, a herald was sent ahead; the executioner hastily released Yuanzhong and told him to rise. Yuanzhong said, "Not knowing whether the edict is genuine, how can I act rashly?"

sentences.zh: 徐待宣敕，然始起謝，觀者鹹歎其臨刑而神色不撓。

translations.literal: He slowly awaited the proclaimed edict, then rose to give thanks; onlookers all sighed at his unshaken bearing facing execution.
translations.idiomatic: He waited calmly for the proclaimed edict, then rose to give thanks; onlookers marveled at his composure facing death.

sentences.zh: 聖曆元年，召授侍御史，擢拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenglü he was summoned and appointed attendant censor, then promoted to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenglü he was summoned as attendant censor, then promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 又為來俊臣、侯思止所陷，再被流於嶺表。

translations.literal: Again he was trapped by Lai Junchen and Hou Sizhi and twice exiled to the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: Again he was framed by Lai Junchen and Hou Sizhi and twice exiled to the south.

sentences.zh: 復還，授御史中丞。

translations.literal: He returned and was appointed vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and was appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 元忠前後三被流，於時人多稱其無罪。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was three times exiled; at the time many called him innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was exiled three times; many at the time said he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 則天嚐謂曰：“卿累負謗鑠，何也？”

translations.literal: Zetian once said to him: "You have repeatedly borne slander—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once asked him, "You have been slandered again and again—why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“臣猶鹿也，羅織之徒，有如獵者，苟須臣肉作羹耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject is like a deer; those who weave nets are like hunters—if they need your subject's flesh for broth."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I am like a deer; those who weave accusations are like hunters—they need my flesh for their stew."

sentences.zh: 此輩殺臣以求達，臣復何辜。”

translations.literal: These men kill your subject to advance—what crime has your subject?"
translations.idiomatic: They kill me to advance—what crime have I committed?"

sentences.zh: 聖曆二年，擢拜鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，檢校并州長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenglü he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, with concurrent duty as prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenglü he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and made Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, with concurrent duty as prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加銀青光祿大夫，遷左肅政台御史大夫，兼檢校洛州長史。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the silver-blue glory grandee rank and moved to censor-in-chief of the Left Bureau for Correcting Governance, with concurrent duty as prefect of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the silver-blue glory grandee rank and became censor-in-chief of the Left Bureau for Correcting Governance, with concurrent duty as prefect of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 政號清嚴。

translations.literal: His administration was known as pure and strict.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was known as pure and strict.

sentences.zh: 長安中，相王為并州元帥，元忠為副。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era, the Prince of Xiang was marshal of Bingzhou and Yuanzhong was his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an era, the Prince of Xiang was marshal of Bingzhou and Yuanzhong was his deputy.

sentences.zh: 時奉宸令張易之嚐縱其家奴淩暴百姓，元忠笞殺之，權豪莫不敬憚。

translations.literal: At that time Attendant Zhang Yizhi often let his household slaves bully the common people; Yuanzhong had them flogged to death, and the powerful all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zhang Yizhi often let his slaves bully the people; Yuanzhong had them flogged to death, and the powerful all feared him.

sentences.zh: 時突厥與吐蕃數犯塞，元忠皆為大總管拒之。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks and Tibetans repeatedly raided the frontier; Yuanzhong served as overall commander to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks and Tibetans repeatedly raided the frontier; Yuanzhong served as overall commander against them.

sentences.zh: 元忠在軍，唯持重自守，竟無所克獲，然亦未嚐敗失。

translations.literal: In the army Yuanzhong only held to caution and self-defense; in the end he won nothing, yet he also never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the field he held to caution; he won no victories, yet never suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 中宗在春宮時，元忠檢校太子左庶子。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace, Yuanzhong served as concurrent Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was crown prince, Yuanzhong served as Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 時張易之、昌宗權寵日盛，傾朝附之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi and Changzong's power and favor grew daily, and the court inclined to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi and Changzong's power grew daily, and the court flocked to them.

sentences.zh: 元忠嚐奏則天曰：“臣承先帝顧眄，受陛下厚恩，不徇忠死節，使小人得在君側，臣之罪也。”

translations.literal: Yuanzhong once memorialized Zetian: "Your subject received the late emperor's gaze and bears Your Majesty's thick kindness; if he does not die loyal to preserve integrity and lets petty men reach the ruler's side, it is your subject's crime."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong once told Empress Wu, "I received the late emperor's favor and Your Majesty's kindness; if I do not die loyal and let petty men reach your side, that is my crime."

sentences.zh: 則天不悅。

translations.literal: Zetian was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 易之、昌宗由是含怒。

translations.literal: Yizhi and Changzong thereby harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and Changzong thereby harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 因則天不豫，乃譖元忠與司禮丞高戩潛謀曰：“主上老矣，吾屬當挾太子而令天下。”

translations.literal: When Zetian was unwell, they slandered Yuanzhong and Director of Rites Gao Jian, saying they secretly plotted: "The ruler is old; we should seize the crown prince and command all under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu fell ill, they slandered Yuanzhong and Director of Rites Gao Jian, claiming they plotted: "The ruler is old; we should seize the crown prince and command the realm."

sentences.zh: 則天惑其言，乃下元忠詔獄，召太子、相王及諸宰相，令昌宗與元忠等殿前參對，反復不決。

translations.literal: Zetian was misled by their words and sent Yuanzhong to imperial prison; she summoned the crown prince, the Prince of Xiang, and all chancellors, and ordered Changzong to confront Yuanzhong and others in the hall—back and forth without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu was misled and imprisoned Yuanzhong; she summoned the crown prince, the Prince of Xiang, and all chancellors, and had Changzong confront Yuanzhong in the hall—without resolution.

sentences.zh: 昌宗又引鳳閣舍人張說令執證元忠。

translations.literal: Changzong again brought Phoenix Pavilion Attendant Zhang Shuo to give testimony against Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong again brought Attendant Zhang Shuo to testify against Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 說初偽許之，及則天召說驗問，說確稱元忠實無此語。

translations.literal: Shuo at first falsely promised, but when Zetian summoned Shuo to examine him, he firmly declared Yuanzhong truly had no such words.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo at first feigned agreement, but when Empress Wu questioned him, he firmly declared Yuanzhong had said no such thing.

sentences.zh: 則天乃悟元忠被誣，然以昌宗之故，特貶授端州高要尉。

translations.literal: Zetian then understood Yuanzhong had been slandered, yet because of Changzong specially demoted him to military adjutant of Gaoyao in Duan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu then saw Yuanzhong had been slandered, yet because of Changzong demoted him to military adjutant of Gaoyao in Duan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，其日驛召元忠，授衛尉卿、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, that same day Yuanzhong was summoned by post and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong took the throne, Yuanzhong was summoned that same day and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 旬日，又遷兵部尚書，知政事如故。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was again promoted to Minister of War, with governance as before.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was promoted to Minister of War, with governance as before.

sentences.zh: 尋進拜侍中，兼檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Palace Attendant, with concurrent duty as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Palace Attendant, with concurrent duty as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 時則天崩，中宗居諒暗，多不視事，軍國大政，獨委元忠者數日。

translations.literal: At that time Zetian had died; Zhongzong was in mourning and for many days did not attend to affairs—great military and civil policy was for several days entrusted to Yuanzhong alone.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu had died; Zhongzong was in mourning and for days did not attend to affairs—military and civil policy was entrusted to Yuanzhong alone.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷中書令，加授光祿大夫，累封齊國公，監修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Director of the Secretariat, given the glory grandee rank, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi in succession, and made supervisor of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Director of the Secretariat, was given the glory grandee rank, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, and made supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，元忠與武三思、祝欽明、徐彥伯、柳衝、韋承慶、崔融、岑羲、徐堅等撰《則天皇后實錄》二十卷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong, Yuanzhong together with Wu Sansi, Zhu Qinming, Xu Yanbo, Liu Chong, Wei Chengqing, Cui Rong, Cen Xi, Xu Jian, and others compiled the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian in twenty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenlong, Yuanzhong with Wu Sansi, Zhu Qinming, Xu Yanbo, Liu Chong, Wei Chengqing, Cui Rong, Cen Xi, Xu Jian, and others compiled the Veritable Record of Empress Zetian in twenty chapters.

sentences.zh: 編次文集一百二十卷奏之。

translations.literal: They arranged and presented a collected literary works in one hundred twenty chapters.
translations.idiomatic: They arranged and presented her collected works in one hundred twenty chapters.

sentences.zh: 中宗稱善，賜元忠物千段，仍封其子衛王府諮議參軍升為任城縣男。

translations.literal: Zhongzong praised it and bestowed on Yuanzhong a thousand lengths of goods; he also enfeoffed his son, Adviser of the Prince of Wei's household Sheng, as Baron of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong praised the work and bestowed a thousand lengths of goods on Yuanzhong; he also enfeoffed his son Sheng, adviser in the Prince of Wei's household, as Baron of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 時元忠特承寵榮，當朝用事。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanzhong especially received favor and glory and held power in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong especially enjoyed favor and held power at court.

sentences.zh: 初元忠作相於則天朝，議者以為公清。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhong first became chancellor in Zetian's court, commentators held him to be fair and pure.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanzhong first became chancellor under Empress Wu, commentators held him fair and upright.

sentences.zh: 至是再居政事，天下莫不延首傾屬，冀有所弘益。

translations.literal: When he again held government affairs, all under heaven craned their necks and inclined to him, hoping he would bring broad benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When he again held power, the realm looked to him with hope that he would bring real benefit.

sentences.zh: 元忠乃親附權豪，抑棄寒俊，竟不能賞善罰惡，勉修時政，議者以此少之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong then personally attached himself to powerful families and suppressed the poor and worthy; in the end he could neither reward good nor punish evil nor strive to repair the politics of the time—commentators therefore thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong then courted the powerful and suppressed the worthy; he neither rewarded good nor punished evil nor strove to reform government—commentators thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，代唐璟為尚書右僕射，兼中書令，仍知兵部尚書事，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year he replaced Tang Jing as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with concurrent duty as Director of the Secretariat, still in charge of the Ministry of War and supervising the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year he replaced Tang Jing as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Director of the Secretariat, still overseeing the Ministry of War and the national history.

sentences.zh: 未幾，元忠請歸鄉拜掃，特賜錦袍一領、銀千兩，並給千騎四人，充其左右，手敕曰：“衣錦晝遊，在乎茲日；

translations.literal: Before long Yuanzhong asked to return home to sweep the tombs; he was specially granted one brocade robe and a thousand taels of silver, with a thousand riders and four men to attend him, and a handwritten edict: "Returning home in brocade to tour by day—may this day be it;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuanzhong asked leave to return home to sweep the tombs; he was granted a brocade robe, a thousand taels of silver, a thousand riders and four attendants, with a handwritten edict: "To tour one's home in brocade by day—let this be that day;"

sentences.zh: 散金敷惠，諒屬斯辰。”

translations.literal: scattering gold to spread favor—surely this is the season."
translations.idiomatic: to scatter gold in generosity—surely this is the season."

sentences.zh: 元忠至鄉里，竟自藏其銀，無所賑施。

translations.literal: When Yuanzhong reached his home district he actually hoarded the silver himself and made no relief distributions.
translations.idiomatic: At home he hoarded the silver and gave nothing to the needy.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝又幸白馬寺以迎勞之，其恩遇如此。

translations.literal: On his return the Emperor again visited White Horse Temple to welcome and reward him—such was his grace.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the Emperor met him at White Horse Temple with such favor.

sentences.zh: 是時，安樂公主嚐私請廢節湣太子，立己為皇太女。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Anle once privately asked to depose Crown Prince Jiemin and install herself as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle once privately asked to depose Crown Prince Jiemin and make herself heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 中宗以問元忠，元忠固稱不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhongzong asked Yuanzhong; Yuanzhong firmly said it could not be done, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong asked Yuanzhong, who firmly refused, and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左僕射，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元忠又嫉武三思專權用事，心常憤歎，思欲誅之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong also resented Wu Sansi's monopolizing power and acting in affairs, and in his heart often sighed in anger, thinking to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong resented Wu Sansi's monopoly of power and longed to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，節湣太子起兵誅三思，元忠及左羽林大將軍李多祚等皆潛預其事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year Crown Prince Jiemin raised troops to execute Sansi; Yuanzhong and Left Feathered Forest General Li Duozuo and others all secretly took part in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year Crown Prince Jiemin raised troops to kill Sansi; Yuanzhong and Left Feathered Forest General Li Duozuo and others secretly joined the plot.

sentences.zh: 太子既斬三思，又率兵詣闕，將請廢韋後為庶人，遇元忠子太仆少卿升於永守門，協令從己。

translations.literal: After the crown prince had beheaded Sansi he again led troops to the palace gate to ask that Empress Wei be deposed to commoner status; he met Yuanzhong's son Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud Sheng at Yongshou Gate and ordered him to follow.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Sansi the crown prince led troops to the palace to depose Empress Wei; he met Yuanzhong's son Sheng, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud, at Yongshou Gate and ordered him to follow.

sentences.zh: 太子兵至玄武樓下，多祚等猶豫不戰，元忠又持兩端，由是不克，升為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's troops reached below the Xuanwu Tower, Duozuo and others hesitated and did not fight; Yuanzhong also held to both sides, and so they could not succeed—Sheng was killed by the mutinous troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuanwu Tower Duozuo and others hesitated; Yuanzhong wavered, and the plot failed—Sheng was killed by the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 中宗以元忠有平寇之功，又素為高宗、天後所禮遇，竟不以升為累，委任如初。

translations.literal: Zhongzong, because Yuanzhong had the merit of pacifying bandits and had long been treated with courtesy by Gaozong and the Heavenly Empress, in the end did not make Sheng a burden on him and entrusted him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong, remembering Yuanzhong's merit and his long favor under Gaozong and Empress Wu, did not blame him for Sheng's death and entrusted him as before.

sentences.zh: 是時，三思之黨兵部尚書宗楚客與侍中紀處訥等又執證元忠及升，雲素與節湣太子同謀構逆，請夷其三族，中宗不許。

translations.literal: At that time Sansi's faction, Minister of War Zong Chuke and Palace Attendant Ji Chune and others, again gave testimony against Yuanzhong and Sheng, saying they had long plotted rebellion with Crown Prince Jiemin and asking to exterminate their three clans; Zhongzong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi's faction, Minister of War Zong Chuke and Palace Attendant Ji Chune, again testified that Yuanzhong and Sheng had long plotted with Crown Prince Jiemin and asked to exterminate their clans; Zhongzong refused.

sentences.zh: 元忠懼不自安，上表固請致仕。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong feared and was ill at ease, and submitted a memorial firmly asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong grew fearful and petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 手製聽解左僕射，以特進、齊國公致仕於家，仍朝朔望。

translations.literal: A handwritten edict allowed him to resign the Left Vice Directorship and retire at home as Special Advanced Grandee and Duke of Qi, still attending court on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed him to resign as Left Vice Director and retire as Special Advanced Grandee and Duke of Qi, still attending on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 楚客等又引右衛郎將姚庭筠為御史中丞，令劾奏元忠，由是貶渠州員外司馬。

translations.literal: Chuke and others again brought Right Guard Commandant Yao Tingyun as vice censor-in-chief to impeach Yuanzhong, and thereby he was demoted to outer assistant in Qú prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke appointed Yao Tingyun vice censor-in-chief to impeach Yuanzhong, and he was demoted to outer assistant in Qú prefecture.

sentences.zh: 侍中楊再思、中書令李嶠皆依楚客之旨，以致元忠之罪，唯中書侍郎蕭至忠正議雲當從寬宥。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yang Zaisi and Director of the Secretariat Li Qiao both followed Chuke's intent to bring Yuanzhong to guilt; only Vice Director of the Secretariat Xiao Zhizhong argued he should receive lenient pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi and Li Qiao followed Chuke to condemn Yuanzhong; only Xiao Zhizhong argued for leniency.

sentences.zh: 楚客大怒，又遣給事中冉祖雍與楊再思奏言：“元忠既緣犯逆，不合更授內地官。”

translations.literal: Chuke was greatly angered and again sent Attendant Reviewer Ran Zuyong with Yang Zaisi to memorialize: "Yuanzhong, having committed treason, should not again be given an inner appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Chuke sent Ran Zuyong and Yang Zaisi to memorialize that Yuanzhong, having committed treason, should not receive an inner appointment.

sentences.zh: 遂左遷思州務川尉。

translations.literal: He was then transferred left to commandant of Wuchuan in Si prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then demoted to commandant of Wuchuan in Si prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頃之，楚客又令御史袁守一奏言：“則天昔在三陽宮不豫，內史狄仁傑奏請陛下監國，元忠密進狀雲不可。

translations.literal: Before long Chuke again ordered Censor Yuan Shouyi to memorialize: "When Zetian was unwell at Sanyang Palace, Inner Scribe Di Renjie memorialized asking Your Majesty to oversee the state; Yuanzhong secretly submitted a memorial saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chuke had Censor Yuan Shouyi memorialize that when Empress Wu was ill at Sanyang Palace, Di Renjie asked Zhongzong to oversee the state while Yuanzhong secretly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 據此，則知元忠懷逆日久，伏請加以嚴誅。”

translations.literal: According to this, one knows Yuanzhong harbored treason for long—your subject prays he receive severe execution."
translations.idiomatic: This proves Yuanzhong long harbored treason—he should be severely punished.

sentences.zh: 中宗謂楊再思等曰：“以朕思之，此是守一大錯。

translations.literal: Zhongzong said to Yang Zaisi and others: "As I consider it, this is Shouyi's great error.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong told Yang Zaisi and others, "As I see it, Shouyi is greatly in error.

sentences.zh: 人臣事主，必在一心，豈有主上少有不安，即請太子知事？

translations.literal: A minister serving his lord must be of one heart—how can there be, when the ruler is slightly unwell, an immediate request that the crown prince handle affairs?
translations.idiomatic: A minister must serve with one heart—when the ruler is slightly unwell, how can one immediately ask the crown prince to govern?

sentences.zh: 乃是狄仁傑樹私惠，未見元忠有失。

translations.literal: This was Di Renjie planting private favor; one does not see that Yuanzhong was at fault.
translations.idiomatic: That was Di Renjie currying private favor; Yuanzhong was not at fault.

sentences.zh: 守一假借前事羅織元忠，豈是道理。”

translations.literal: Shouyi, borrowing past affairs, weaves nets around Yuanzhong—how is this reasonable?"
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi, using past events, frames Yuanzhong—how is that reasonable?"

sentences.zh: 楚客等遂止。

translations.literal: Chuke and others thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke and others thereupon desisted.

sentences.zh: 元忠行至涪陵而卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong died on the road at Fuling, aged over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong died at Fuling on the road, aged over seventy.

sentences.zh: 韋安石，京兆萬年人，周大司空、鄖國公孝寬曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wei Anshi was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao, great-grandson of Zhou Grand Minister of Works and Duke of Yun, Wei Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi came from Wannian in Jingzhao, great-grandson of Zhou Grand Minister of Works and Duke of Yun, Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 祖津，大業末為民部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jin, at the end of the Daye era, was Vice Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jin, at the end of the Daye era, was Vice Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 煬帝之幸江都，敕津與段達、元文都等於洛陽留守，仍檢校民部尚書事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang went to Jiangdu, he ordered Jin together with Duan Da, Yuan Wenshu, and others to remain at Luoyang on guard, with concurrent duty inspecting the Ministry of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang went to Jiangdu, he left Jin with Duan Da, Yuan Wenshu, and others to guard Luoyang, with concurrent duty over the Ministry of the Household.

sentences.zh: 李密逼東都，津拒戰於上東門外。

translations.literal: Li Mi pressed the eastern capital; Jin resisted in battle outside the Shangdong Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi pressed the eastern capital; Jin fought him outside the Shangdong Gate.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，為密所囚，及王世充殺文都等，津獨免其難。

translations.literal: His army was defeated and he was taken prisoner by Mi; when Wang Shichong killed Wenshu and others, Jin alone escaped the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he was taken by Mi; when Wang Shichong killed Wenshu and others, Jin alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 密敗，歸東都，世充僭號，深被委遇。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated he returned to the eastern capital; Shichong usurped the throne and deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi's defeat he returned to Luoyang; Shichong usurped the throne and deeply trusted him.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽平，高祖與津有舊，征授諫議大夫，檢校黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, Gaozu, having old ties with Jin, summoned and appointed him Remonstrator and Reviewer and concurrent Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, Gaozu, who knew Jin of old, appointed him Remonstrator and Reviewer and concurrent Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 出為陵州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Ling prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ling prefecture and died there.

sentences.zh: 父琬，成州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wan was prefect of Cheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan was prefect of Cheng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 叔琨，戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His uncle Kun was Vice Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Kun was Vice Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 琨弟遂，倉部員外。

translations.literal: Kun's younger brother Sui was Outer Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's younger brother Sui was Outer Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 安石應明經舉，累授乾封尉，蘇良嗣甚禮之。

translations.literal: Anshi passed the classics examination and was appointed in succession as Qianfeng Assistant; Su Liangsi greatly honored him.
