translations.idiomatic: Anshi passed the classics examination and became Qianfeng Assistant; Su Liangsi greatly honored him.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，三遷雍州司兵，良嗣時為文昌左相，謂安石曰：“大材須大用，何為徒勞於州縣也。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang he was thrice promoted to Yongzhou Arms Officer; Liangsi was then Left Chancellor of the Secretariat and said to Anshi: "Great timber needs great use—why toil in vain at prefectures and counties?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang he rose thrice to Yongzhou Arms Officer; Liangsi, then Left Chancellor, told him, "Great timber needs great use—why waste yourself in county posts?"

sentences.zh: 特薦於則天，擢拜膳部員外郎、永昌令、并州司馬。

translations.literal: He specially recommended him to Zetian, who promoted him to Outer Assistant in the Ministry of Provisions, Magistrate of Yongchang, and Bingzhou Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Anshi to Empress Wu, who promoted him to Outer Assistant in the Ministry of Provisions, Magistrate of Yongchang, and Vice Director of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 則天手製勞之曰：“聞卿在彼，庶事存心，善政表於能官，仁明彰於鎮撫。

translations.literal: Zetian wrote by hand to comfort him: "I hear that at your post you keep all affairs in mind, good government shown in capable office, benevolence and clarity displayed in pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu wrote by hand to praise him: "I hear that at your post you attend to all affairs, govern well, and rule with benevolence and clarity.

sentences.zh: 如此稱職，深慰朕懷。”

translations.literal: Such fulfillment of duty deeply comforts Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: Such service deeply comforts me."

sentences.zh: 俄拜并州刺史，又曆德、鄭二州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Prefect of Bingzhou and in turn Prefect of De and Zheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Prefect of Bingzhou, then of De and Zheng prefectures.

sentences.zh: 安石性持重，少言笑，為政清嚴，所在人吏鹹畏憚之。

translations.literal: Anshi's nature was grave; he spoke and laughed little; his government was pure and strict, and wherever he was, officials and people all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was grave, spoke little, and governed with purity and strictness; wherever he served, officials and people feared him.

sentences.zh: 久視年，遷文昌右丞，尋拜鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the Jiushi era he was moved to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon he was made Vice Director of the Crane Terrace, Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, and concurrent Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiushi era he became Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Vice Director of the Crane Terrace and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, with concurrent duty as Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，為神都留守，兼判天官、秋官二尚書事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an he was Divine Capital Guardian, with concurrent duty judging the Ministries of Astronomy and Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chang'an he was Divine Capital Guardian, with concurrent duty over the Ministries of Astronomy and Punishments.

sentences.zh: 後與崔神慶等同為侍讀，尋知納言事。

translations.literal: Later he served with Cui Shenqing and others as Lecturer, and soon was in charge of the Office of the Master of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lectured with Cui Shenqing and others, and soon oversaw the Office of the Master of Documents.

sentences.zh: 是歲，又加檢校中台左丞，兼太子左庶子、鳳閣鸞台三品如故。

translations.literal: That year he was also given concurrent duty as Vice Director of the Left Platform of the Central Office, with Left Vice Director of the Crown Prince and Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace Third Rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was also made Vice Director of the Left Platform with his previous ranks unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時張易之兄弟及武三思皆恃寵用權，安石數折辱之，甚為易之等所忌。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi's brothers and Wu Sansi all relied on favor to wield power; Anshi several times humiliated them and was deeply resented by Yizhi and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi's brothers and Wu Sansi relied on favor for power; Anshi several times humiliated them and was deeply resented.

sentences.zh: 嚐於內殿賜宴，易之引蜀商宋霸子等數人於前博戲。

translations.literal: Once at an inner-hall banquet Yizhi brought Shu merchants Song Bazi and several others before him to gamble.
translations.idiomatic: At an inner banquet Yizhi brought Shu merchants including Song Bazi to gamble before the throne.

sentences.zh: 安石疏奏曰：“蜀商等賤類，不合預登此筵。”

translations.literal: Anshi submitted a memorial: "Shu merchants and other base sorts should not be allowed to ascend this feast."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi memorialized, "Shu merchants and other base sorts should not attend this feast."

sentences.zh: 因顧左右令逐出之，座者皆為失色。

translations.literal: He then looked to the left and right and ordered them driven out; those seated all changed color.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them driven out; all at table turned pale.

sentences.zh: 則天以安石辭直，深慰勉之。

translations.literal: Zetian, because Anshi's words were straight, deeply comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, finding his words straight, deeply praised and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 時鳳閣侍郎陸元方在座，退而告人曰：“此真宰相，非吾等所及也。”

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Lu Yuanfang was seated; afterward he told others: "This is a true chancellor—not our equal."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Lu Yuanfang, seated there, later said, "This is a true chancellor—not our equal."

sentences.zh: 則天嚐幸興泰宮，欲就捷路，安石奏曰：“千金之子，且有垂堂之誡，萬乘之尊，不宜輕乘危險。

translations.literal: Zetian once visited Xingtai Palace and wished to take a shortcut; Anshi memorialized: "The son of a thousand gold has the warning against sitting beneath the hall eaves; the lord of ten thousand chariots should not lightly ride danger.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu once wished to take a shortcut to Xingtai Palace; Anshi memorialized, "Even the son of a wealthy house is warned against sitting beneath the eaves; the sovereign should not lightly court danger.

sentences.zh: 此路板築初成，無自然之固，鑾駕經之，臣等敢不請罪。”

translations.literal: This road's planking was newly built without natural solidity; if the imperial carriage passes it, your subject and others dare not escape guilt."
translations.idiomatic: This road was newly built and not naturally firm; if Your Majesty's carriage passes, we dare not escape blame."

sentences.zh: 則天登時為之回輦。

translations.literal: Zetian at once turned the carriage back for him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu at once turned her carriage back.

sentences.zh: 安石俄又舉奏易之等罪狀，初有敕付安石及夏官尚書唐休璟推問，未竟而事變。

translations.literal: Anshi soon again memorialized the crimes of Yizhi and others; at first there was an edict ordering Anshi and Minister of Summer Offices Tang Xiujing to investigate, but before it was finished affairs changed.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi soon memorialized Yizhi's crimes; an edict ordered him and Tang Xiujing to investigate, but before it finished affairs changed.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，征拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was summoned as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shenlong he was summoned as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 是歲，又遷吏部尚書，復知政事。

translations.literal: That year he was again moved to Minister of Personnel and again knew government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became Minister of Personnel and again held power.

sentences.zh: 俄代張柬之為中書令，封鄖國公，以嚐為宮僚，賜實封三百戶，又兼相王府長史。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Zhang Jianzhi as Director of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Duke of Yun, and because he had once been a palace officer was granted three hundred households of actual fief; he was also concurrent Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Zhang Jianzhi as Director of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Duke of Yun, granted three hundred households of fief as a former palace officer, and became Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xiang's household.

sentences.zh: 俄轉戶部尚書，復為侍中，監修國史。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Minister of the Household and again became Palace Attendant, supervising the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Minister of the Household and again Palace Attendant, supervising the national history.

sentences.zh: 中宗與庶人嚐因正月十五日夜幸其第，賜賚不可勝數。

translations.literal: Zhongzong and the commoner consort once on the fifteenth night of the first month visited his residence; gifts beyond counting were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong and Empress Wei once visited his home on the Lantern Festival night with gifts beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 又中宗嚐幸安樂公主城西池館，公主具舟楫，請禦樓船，安石諫曰：“禦輕舟，乘不測，臣恐非帝王之事。”

translations.literal: Again Zhongzong once visited Princess Anle's western-city pool and lodge; the princess prepared boats and asked to board the tower ship. Anshi remonstrated: "Riding light boats and taking the unforeseen—your subject fears this is not an affair for emperors and kings."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong once visited Princess Anle's western lodge; she prepared boats and asked to board the tower ship. Anshi remonstrated, "Light boats and unforeseen waters are not fit for a sovereign."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: It stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，拜太子少保，改封郇國公。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and his fief was changed to Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne he became Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 俄又歷侍中、中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he again served in turn as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again served as Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was given the rank of Grandee with the Opening of an Office and Equal Treatment to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun he was given Grandee with the Opening of an Office and Equal Treatment to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主與竇懷貞等潛有異圖，將引安石預其事，公主屢使子婿唐晙邀安石至宅，安石竟拒而不往。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Taiping and Dou Huaizhen and others secretly had different designs and wished to draw Anshi into the affair; the princess several times sent her son-in-law Tang Jun to invite Anshi to her residence, but Anshi ultimately refused and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping and Dou Huaizhen secretly plotted and tried to draw Anshi in; the princess repeatedly sent her son-in-law Tang Jun to invite him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 睿宗嚐密召安石，謂曰：“聞朝廷傾心東宮，卿何不察也？”

translations.literal: Ruizong once secretly summoned Anshi and said to him: "I hear the court inclines its heart to the Eastern Palace—why do you not investigate?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong once secretly summoned him and said, "I hear the court favors the Eastern Palace—why do you not investigate?"

sentences.zh: 安石對曰：“陛下何得亡國之言，此必太平之計。

translations.literal: Anshi replied: "Your Majesty, how can you speak words that would lose the state? This must be Taiping's scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi replied, "Your Majesty, how can you speak words that would lose the state? This must be the Princess's scheme.

sentences.zh: 太子有大功於社稷，仁明孝友，天下所稱，願陛下無信讒言以致惑也。”

translations.literal: The crown prince has great merit for the altars of soil and grain, benevolent, bright, and filial, praised by all under heaven—I pray Your Majesty not believe slanderous words and fall into confusion."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince has great merit, is benevolent, bright, and filial, and is praised by all—I pray Your Majesty not believe slander."

sentences.zh: 睿宗矍然曰：“朕知之矣，卿勿言也。”

translations.literal: Ruizong started and said: "I understand; do not speak further."
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong started and said, "I understand; speak no more."

sentences.zh: 太平於簾中竊聽之，乃構飛語，欲令鞫之，賴郭元振保護獲免。

translations.literal: Taiping listened secretly behind the curtain and thereupon fabricated flying rumors, wishing to have him interrogated; thanks to Guo Yuanzhen's protection he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping listened behind the curtain and fabricated rumors to have him interrogated; Guo Yuanzhen protected him.

sentences.zh: 俄而遷尚書左僕射，兼太子賓客，依舊同中書門下三品，雖假以崇寵，實去其權。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Tutor of the Crown Prince, still Associate Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery Third Rank; though outwardly given lofty favor, in fact his power was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Left Vice Director and Tutor of the Crown Prince, still Third Rank chancellor; though honored in name, his power was removed.

sentences.zh: 其冬，罷知政事，拜特進，充東都留守。

translations.literal: That winter he ceased knowing government affairs, was appointed Special Advanced Grandee, and made Eastern Capital Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he left government, became Special Advanced Grandee, and was made Eastern Capital Guardian.

sentences.zh: 太常主簿李元澄，即安石之子婿，其妻病死，安石夫人薛氏疑元澄先所幸婢厭殺之。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Li Yuancheng was Anshi's son-in-law; his wife died of illness and Anshi's wife Lady Xue suspected Yuancheng's former favored maid had killed her by curse.
translations.idiomatic: Director Li Yuancheng was Anshi's son-in-law; when his wife died Lady Xue suspected a former maid had killed her by curse.

sentences.zh: 其婢久已轉嫁，薛氏使人捕而捶之致死。

translations.literal: The maid had long since been remarried; Lady Xue sent men to seize and beat her to death.
translations.idiomatic: The maid had long been remarried; Lady Xue had her seized and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 由是為御史中丞楊茂謙所劾，出為蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereby he was impeached by Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Maoqian and sent out as Prefect of Pu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yang Maoqian impeached him and he was sent out as Prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉青州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Prefect of Qing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to Prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 安石初在蒲州時，太常卿薑皎有所請托，安石拒之，皎大怒。

translations.literal: When Anshi was first at Pu, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao made a request that Anshi refused; Jiao was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: At Pu, Director Jiang Jiao made a request Anshi refused; Jiao was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，皎弟晦為御史中丞，以安石等作相時，同受中宗遺製，宗楚客、韋溫削除相王輔政之辭，安石不能正其事，令侍御史洪子輿舉劾之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, Jiao's younger brother Hui was vice censor-in-chief; because when Anshi and others were chancellors they had all received Zhongzong's testamentary edict, Zong Chuke and Wei Wen had deleted the words on the Prince of Xiang's assisting in government, and Anshi could not correct the matter, he ordered Attendant Censor Hong Ziyu to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 2, Jiao's brother Hui was vice censor-in-chief; because when Anshi was chancellor he had received Zhongzong's testament, and Zong Chuke and Wei Wen had deleted the Prince of Xiang's role in assisting government without Anshi correcting it, Hui ordered Hong Ziyu to impeach them.

sentences.zh: 子輿以事經赦令，固稱不可。

translations.literal: Ziyu, because the matter had passed under an amnesty edict, firmly said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu said the matter was covered by amnesty and refused.

sentences.zh: 監察御史郭震希皎等意，越次奏之，於是下詔曰：“青州刺史韋安石、太子賓客韋嗣立、刑部尚書趙彥昭等，往在先朝，曲蒙厚賞，因緣幸會，久在廟堂，朋黨比周，聞於行路。

translations.literal: Supervisory Censor Guo Zhen, hoping to please Jiao and the rest, skipped rank to memorialize; thereupon an edict said: "Qing prefecture Prefect Wei Anshi, Tutor of the Crown Prince Wei Sili, Minister of Punishments Zhao Yanzhao, and others, in the former court wrongly received thick reward; by fortunate coincidence they long remained in the temple hall, forming factions heard on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory Censor Guo Zhen, pleasing Jiao, skipped rank to memorialize; an edict said, "Prefect Wei Anshi, Tutor Wei Sili, Minister Zhao Yanzhao, and others long held power in the former court, forming factions heard on every road.

sentences.zh: 景龍之末，長蛇縱禍，倉卒之間，人神憤怨，未聞舍生取義，直道昌言，遂削太上皇輔政之辭，用韋氏臨朝之策。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinglong the long snake unleashed calamity; in the haste between, gods and men were angry, yet one did not hear of giving life to take righteousness or speaking straight to expand the Way—they then deleted the Supreme Emperor's words on assisting in government and used the Wei clan's policy of holding court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jinglong disaster struck; gods and men were angry, yet they did not speak straight—they deleted the retired emperor's words on assisting government and used the Wei clan's policy of holding court.

sentences.zh: 比常隱忍，復以崇班，將期愧畏，稍懲前惡，而尚款回邪，苟安榮寵。

translations.literal: They usually concealed this and again received lofty rank, hoping shame and fear would slightly chastise past evil—yet they still treated crooked ways with warmth and clung to glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: They concealed this and again received rank, yet still clung to crooked ways and favor.

sentences.zh: 宜從謫官之典，以勵事君之節。

translations.literal: They should follow the canon of demoted officials to encourage the integrity of serving one's lord."
translations.idiomatic: They should be demoted to encourage loyalty to one's lord."

sentences.zh: 安石可沔州別駕，嗣立可岳州別駕，彥昭可袁州別駕，並員外置。”

translations.literal: Anshi could be Military Adjutant of Mian prefecture, Sili Military Adjutant of Yue prefecture, Yanzhao Military Adjutant of Yuan prefecture—all outer appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was made Military Adjutant of Mian, Sili of Yue, Yanzhao of Yuan—all outer posts.

sentences.zh: 安石既至沔州，晦又奏云：“安石嚐檢校定陵造作，隱官物入己。”

translations.literal: After Anshi reached Mian, Hui again memorialized: "Anshi once inspected construction at Ding Mausoleum and hid official goods for himself."
translations.idiomatic: At Mian, Hui memorialized that Anshi had hidden official goods while inspecting Ding Mausoleum construction.

sentences.zh: 敕符下州征贓。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the prefecture to collect the illicit goods.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the prefecture to collect the goods.

sentences.zh: 安石歎曰：“此祇應須我死耳！”

translations.literal: Anshi sighed: "This simply means I must die!"
translations.idiomatic: Anshi sighed, "This simply means I must die!"

sentences.zh: 憤激而卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died in anger and agitation, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in anger and agitation, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，贈蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan he was posthumously given Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 17 he was posthumously made Prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，以子貴，追贈開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射、郇國公，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, because of his son's honor he was posthumously given Grandee with Opening of an Office, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Duke of Xun, with posthumous title Cultured and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, because of his son's honor, he was posthumously given Grandee with Opening of an Office, Left Vice Director, Duke of Xun, with posthumous title Cultured and Upright.

sentences.zh: 二子陟、斌，並早知名。

translations.literal: His two sons Zhi and Bin were both early known by name.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Zhi and Bin were both known early for their talent.

sentences.zh: 陟字殷卿，代為關中著姓，人物衣冠，弈世榮盛。

translations.literal: Zhi's courtesy name was Yinqing; his family for generations had been a prominent surname in Guanzhong, and its members in person and dress had enjoyed glory and prosperity age after age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Yinqing, came from a family long numbered among the eminent clans of Guanzhong—refined in bearing, distinguished in rank, and prosperous through the generations.

sentences.zh: 安石晚有子，及為并州司馬，始生陟及斌，俱少聰敏，頗異常童。

translations.literal: Anshi had sons late in life; when he became Administrator of Bingzhou, Zhi and Bin were born. Both were clever and keen from childhood, quite unlike ordinary children.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi became a father only in his later years. While serving as military aide in Bingzhou he had Zhi and Bin, both precocious boys who stood apart even among gifted children.

sentences.zh: 陟自幼風標整峻，獨立不群，安石尤愛之。

translations.literal: From childhood Zhi's bearing was upright and lofty; he stood apart from the crowd, and Anshi loved him especially.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi carried himself with a grave, dignified bearing even as a boy, aloof from his peers—and Anshi doted on him above all.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，安石為中書令，陟始十歲，拜溫王府東閣祭酒，加朝散大夫，累遷秘書太堂丞，有文彩，善隸書，辭人、秀士已遊其門矣。

translations.literal: In Shenlong 2, when Anshi was Zhongshu Ling, Zhi was only ten. He was appointed Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Wen's household and given the rank of Chaosan Daifu. He rose through the ranks to Assistant Director in the Secretariat Grand Hall. He had literary talent, was skilled at clerical script, and literary men and talented scholars already visited his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 2, when Anshi was chief minister, the ten-year-old Zhi was made libationer of the eastern pavilion in the Prince of Wen's household and given the rank of Chaosan Daifu. He rose to assistant director in the Secretariat, showed real literary gifts, and wrote an elegant clerical hand; poets and promising scholars were already calling at his door.

sentences.zh: 開元初，丁父憂，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he entered mourning for his father and observed the mourning rites with more than customary rigor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaiyuan era he entered mourning for his father and observed the rites with more than customary rigor.

sentences.zh: 自此杜門不出八年，與弟斌相勸勵，探討典墳，不舍晝夜，文華當代，俱有盛名。

translations.literal: From then on he shut his door and did not go out for eight years. He and his brother Bin encouraged each other, studied the canonical texts, and did not cease day or night. Their literary brilliance was the finest of their age, and both enjoyed great fame.
translations.idiomatic: For eight years he kept his doors closed. He and his brother Bin spurred each other on, poring over the classics without rest by day or night, until both won contemporary fame for their literary brilliance.

sentences.zh: 於時才名之士王維、崔顥、盧象等，常與陟唱和遊處。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Wei, Cui Hao, Lu Xiang, and other men of talent and fame often exchanged verse with Zhi and kept his company.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, Cui Hao, Lu Xiang, and other leading literary names of the day often exchanged verse with Zhi and kept his company.

sentences.zh: 廣平宋公見陟歎曰：“盛德遺範，盡在是矣。”」

translations.literal: Lord Song of Guangping saw Zhi and sighed, saying: "The splendid virtue and worthy legacy are all in this one."
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Song of Guangping met Zhi he exclaimed, "The great virtue and worthy example of the clan are embodied in this lad alone."

sentences.zh: 暦洛陽令，轉吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He served as Magistrate of Luoyang and was transferred to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Luoyang, then moved to bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 張九齡一代辭宗，爲中書令，引陟爲中書舍人，與孫逖、梁渉對掌文誥，時人以爲美談。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling, the literary master of an age, as Zhongshu Ling brought Zhi in as Zhongshu Sheren. With Sun Su and Liang She he jointly handled imperial edicts, and people considered it a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling, the reigning master of prose, as chief minister brought Zhi in as a drafting official. Zhi shared charge of imperial edicts with Sun Su and Liang She—a pairing the age spoke of with admiration.

sentences.zh: 後爲禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He later became vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 陟好接後輩，尤鑒於文，雖辭人後生，靡不諳練。

translations.literal: Zhi liked receiving juniors and was especially discerning in literature; even young literary men, there was none he did not know well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi delighted in cultivating younger talent and had an especially keen eye for writing; he knew every aspiring poet of the day.

sentences.zh: 曩者主司取與，皆以一場之善，登其科目，不盡其才。

translations.literal: Formerly the chief examiners in selection all relied on excellence in one session to advance candidates to rank and did not exhaust their talent.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the examiners had promoted candidates on the strength of a single good performance and thus failed to measure their full ability.

sentences.zh: 陟先責舊，仍令舉人自通所工詩筆，先試一日，知其所長，然後依常式考核，片善無遺，美聲盈路。

translations.literal: Zhi first rebuked the old practice, then ordered candidates to declare their skilled poetry and prose, first tested them for one day to know their strengths, and then followed the regular form of examination. Not a spark of talent was missed, and praise filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi first rebuked the old practice, then had every candidate declare his strengths in verse and prose and sit a preliminary day-long trial so he could see what each did best before the formal examination. No merit went unrecognized, and his reputation spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 後為吏部侍郎，常病選人冒名接腳，闕員既少，取士良難，正調者被擠，偽集者冒進。

translations.literal: Later, as Vice Minister of Personnel, he was often troubled that candidates falsely assumed names and stepped into vacant posts. With so few openings, selecting worthy men was very hard: legitimate appointees were crowded out while impostors pushed ahead.
translations.idiomatic: As vice minister of personnel he deplored the practice whereby candidates falsely assumed vacant posts or "foot-in" slots: with so few openings, finding worthy men was hard—legitimate appointees were squeezed out while impostors pushed ahead.

sentences.zh: 陟剛腸嫉惡，風彩嚴正，選人疑其有瑕，案聲盤詰，無不首伏。

translations.literal: Zhi had an upright nature that hated evil; his bearing was stern and correct. When candidates were suspected of flaws, he rapped the desk and questioned them, and all confessed without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and upright by nature, Zhi confronted every candidate who looked dubious: at his desk, with a sharp rap and relentless questioning, all eventually confessed.

sentences.zh: 每歲皆贖得數百員闕，以待淹滯，常謂所親曰：“使陟知銓衡一二年，則無人可選矣。”

translations.literal: Each year he recovered hundreds of improper appointments to wait for the long-stalled. He often told intimates, saying: "If Zhi managed selection for one or two years, there would be no one left to select."
translations.idiomatic: Each year he recovered hundreds of improper appointments to give long-waiting candidates their chance. He often told friends, "Let me run the board of appointments for a year or two, and there will be nobody left worth selecting."

sentences.zh: 陟門地豪華，早踐清列，侍兒閹閽，列侍左右者十數，衣書藥食，鹹有典掌，而輿馬僮奴，勢侔於王家主第。

translations.literal: Zhi's family status was luxurious; he had early entered the ranks of the pure and lofty. Serving maids and eunuch doorkeepers, a dozen lined up at his left and right. Clothes, books, medicine, and food all had dedicated stewards, while his carriages, horses, and page boys rivaled a princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi came from great wealth and entered high office young. A dozen maids and chamber attendants waited at his side; stewards managed his wardrobe, library, medicine, and meals; his equipage, horses, and servants rivaled a princely house.

sentences.zh: 自以才地人物，坐取三公，頗以簡貴自處，善誘納後進，其同列朝要，視之蔑如也。

translations.literal: He considered that with his talent, pedigree, and person he would simply take one of the Three Ducal offices. He rather kept himself aloof and noble, was good at guiding juniors, but looked on his fellow court grandees with disdain.
translations.idiomatic: Confident that his talent, pedigree, and person destined him for one of the Three Ducal offices, he held himself loftily aloof. He was generous with younger men, but regarded his peers among the high ministers with thinly veiled contempt.

sentences.zh: 如道義相知，靡隔貴賤，而布衣韋帶之士，恒虛席倒屣以迎之，時人以此稱重。

translations.literal: If knowing each other in righteousness, there was no barrier between noble and low; for common scholars in hemp sashes he always emptied a seat and overturned his shoes to welcome them, and people praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Where friendship was grounded in principle he made no distinction of rank. For plain scholars in hemp sashes he would always clear a seat and rush out shoeless to receive them—conduct for which the age honored him.

sentences.zh: 李林甫忌之，出為襄陽太守，兼本道采訪使，又改陳留采訪使，復加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Li Linfu resented him and had him sent out as Prefect of Xiangyang, also Circuit Investigating Commissioner, then changed to Chenliu Investigating Commissioner, and again given the rank of Yinqing Guanglu Daifu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu resented him and had him sent out as prefect of Xiangyang and commissioner for the circuit, then reassigned as commissioner for Chenliu, with the additional rank of Yinqing Guanglu Daifu.

sentences.zh: 天寶中襲封郇國公，以親累貶鍾離太守，重貶義陽太守。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he inherited the title Duke of Xun, then was demoted to Prefect of Zhongli because of kin association, and demoted again to Prefect of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he inherited the title Duke of Xun, then was demoted to prefect of Zhongli because of kin association, and demoted again to prefect of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 尋移河東太守，充本道采訪使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Hedong and filled the post of Circuit Investigating Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Hedong as prefect and circuit commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十二年入考，在華清宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he came in for his performance review at Huaqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he came in for his performance review at Huaqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 右相楊國忠惡其才望，恐踐台衡，乃引河東人吳象之謂曰：“子能使人告陟乎？

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Right Yang Guozhong hated Zhi's talent and reputation and feared he might reach the top of government. He summoned Wu Xiangzhi of Hedong and said: "Can you have someone denounce Zhi?"
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of the Right Yang Guozhong hated Zhi's ability and reputation and feared he might reach the top of government. He summoned Wu Xiangzhi of Hedong and asked, "Can you get someone to accuse Zhi?"

sentences.zh: 吾以子為御史。”

translations.literal: I will make you a censor.
translations.idiomatic: I'll make you a censor.

sentences.zh: 象之曰：“能。”

translations.literal: Xiangzhi said: "I can."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiangzhi replied, "I can."

sentences.zh: 乃告陟與御史中丞吉溫結托，欲謀陷朝廷，又誘陟侄韋元誌證之。

translations.literal: He then denounced Zhi for collusion with Censor-in-Chief Ji Wen in a plot against the court, and also induced Zhi's nephew Wei Yuanzhi to testify.
translations.idiomatic: He duly denounced Zhi for collusion with the censor-in-chief Ji Wen in a plot against the throne, and induced Zhi's nephew Wei Yuanzhi to corroborate the charge.

sentences.zh: 陟坐貶為桂州桂嶺尉，未之任，再貶昭州平樂尉。

translations.literal: Zhi was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Guilin in Guizhou. Before he could take up the post he was demoted again to Assistant Magistrate of Pingle in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was demoted to assistant magistrate of Guilin in Guizhou; before he could take up the post he was demoted again to assistant magistrate of Pingle in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 會祿山反，陷洛陽，陟愛弟斌為賊所得。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled and took Luoyang, Zhi's beloved younger brother Bin was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled and took Luoyang, Zhi's beloved younger brother Bin fell into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 國忠欲構陟與賊通應，潛令吏卒伺其所居，欲協之令陟憂死。

translations.literal: Guozhong wanted to frame Zhi as communicating with the rebels, secretly ordered clerks and soldiers to watch his dwelling, and wanted to coerce him to die from worry.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhong tried to frame Zhi for colluding with the rebels, secretly posting officials to watch his residence in the hope of driving him to death by grief.

sentences.zh: 其士豪人勸陟曰：“昔張燕公竄逐，藏於陳氏，以免危亡。

translations.literal: Local gentry urged Zhi, saying: "Formerly the Duke of Yan fled in exile and hid with the Chen clan to escape peril and death."
translations.idiomatic: Local worthies urged Zhi: "When Duke Yan of Zhang was driven into exile he took shelter with the Chen clan and so escaped with his life."

sentences.zh: 詔命儻來，誰敢申覆？

translations.literal: If an edict should come, who would dare appeal?
translations.idiomatic: If an imperial order comes down, who dares appeal?

sentences.zh: 未若輕舟千里，且泛溪洞，候事清徐出，豈不美也！”

translations.literal: Better to take a light boat a thousand li, drift among streams and caves, wait until things clear and emerge leisurely—would that not be fine!
translations.idiomatic: Better take a light boat far away and hide among the rivers and caverns until the storm passes—would that not be wise?

sentences.zh: 陟慨然應之曰：“我積信於國朝，非一代也。

translations.literal: Zhi sighed and replied, saying: "I have accumulated trust in the dynastic court, not for one generation alone."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered with deep feeling: "My family has built up the dynasty's trust over generations—not just one reign."

sentences.zh: 況素所秉心，無負神理，命之合爾，其敢逃刑？

translations.literal: Moreover what I have always held in my heart owes nothing to divine principle; if fate so decrees, how dare I flee punishment?
translations.idiomatic: My conscience is clear before Heaven. If this is my appointed end, how dare I flee the law?

sentences.zh: 燕公之謀，誠愧厚意，不能從也。”

translations.literal: The Duke of Yan's plan truly shames me for its kind intent, but I cannot follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gong's scheme shames me for its goodwill, but I cannot accept it.

sentences.zh: 因謝遣之，乃堅臥不動。

translations.literal: So he thanked them and sent them away, then lay firm and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: He thanked them and sent them away, then lay still and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 經歲餘，潼關失守，肅宗即位於靈武，起為吳郡太守，兼江南東道采訪使。

translations.literal: After more than a year Tong Pass fell. When Suzong took the throne at Lingwu, Zhi was recalled as Prefect of Wu and Commissioner for Jiangnan East.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Tong Pass fell. When Suzong took the throne at Lingwu, Zhi was recalled as prefect of Wu and commissioner for Jiangnan East.

sentences.zh: 未到郡，肅宗使中官賈遊嚴手詔追之。

translations.literal: Before he reached the commandery, Suzong sent the eunuch Jia Youyan with a handwritten edict to recall him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post, Suzong sent the eunuch Jia Youyan with a handwritten edict summoning him back.

sentences.zh: 未至鳳翔，會江東永王擅起兵，令陟招諭，除御史大夫，兼江東節度使。

translations.literal: Before he reached Fengxiang, Prince Yong of Jiangdong had raised troops on his own authority. Zhi was ordered to win over the region, appointed Censor-in-Chief, and also Military Commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Fengxiang, Prince Yong of Jiangdong had raised troops on his own authority. Zhi was ordered to win over the region, appointed censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 陟以季廣琛從永王下江，非其本意，懼罪出奔，未有所適，乃有表請拜廣琛為丹陽太守、兼御史中丞、緣江防禦使，以安反側。

translations.literal: Because Ji Guangchen had followed Prince Yong downriver, not his original intent, he feared guilt and fled with nowhere to go. Zhi submitted a memorial requesting that Guangchen be appointed Prefect of Danyang, also Vice Censor-in-Chief and River-Defense Commissioner, to pacify the wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Guangchen, who had followed Prince Yong downriver, had not meant to rebel but fled in fear of punishment with nowhere to go. Zhi memorialized that Guangchen be made prefect of Danyang, vice censor-in-chief, and river-defense commissioner to reassure the discontented.

sentences.zh: 因與淮南節度使高適、淮西節度使來瑱等同至安州。

translations.literal: Then with Huainan Military Commissioner Gao Shi and Huaixi Military Commissioner Lai Tian he together reached Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then went with Huainan commissioner Gao Shi and Huaixi commissioner Lai Tian to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 陟謂適、瑱曰：“今中原未復，江淮動搖，人心安危，實在茲日。

translations.literal: Zhi said to Shi and Tian: "Today the Central Plains are not yet recovered, the Jiang-Huai region is shaken, and the safety or peril of men's hearts truly rests on this day."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said to Shi and Tian, "The heartland is still unreclaimed and the Jiang-Huai region trembles. The fate of men's loyalty hangs on what we do today."

sentences.zh: 若不齊盟質信，以示四方，令知三帥協心，萬里同力，則難以集事矣。”

translations.literal: If we do not form an alliance with pledged faith to show the four directions, let them know the three commanders are of one heart and ten thousand li of one force, then it will be hard to gather affairs together.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we bind ourselves in sworn alliance and show the realm that the three commanders speak with one voice across a thousand miles, we cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 陟推瑱為地主，乃為載書，登壇誓眾曰：“淮西節度使、兼御史大夫瑱，江東節度使、御史大夫陟，淮南節度使、御史大夫適等，銜國威命，各鎮方隅，糾合三垂，翦除凶慝，好惡同之，無有異志。

translations.literal: Zhi proposed Tian as host and drew up a covenant. Ascending the altar he swore before the assembly, saying: "Huaixi Military Commissioner and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief Tian, Jiangdong Military Commissioner and Censor-in-Chief Zhi, Huainan Military Commissioner and Censor-in-Chief Shi and others, bearing the august mandate of the state, each guarding a region, gathering the three frontiers, cutting down the wicked and vicious—we share the same likes and dislikes and have no divergent intent."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi proposed Tian as host of the ceremony and drafted a covenant. Mounting the altar he swore before the assembly: "Huaixi commissioner and concurrent censor-in-chief Lai Tian, Jiangdong commissioner and censor-in-chief Wei Zhi, Huainan commissioner and censor-in-chief Gao Shi—we bear the imperial mandate, each guarding our sector, rallying the three frontiers and cutting down the wicked. Our aims are one and our hearts united."

sentences.zh: 有渝此盟，墜命亡族。

translations.literal: Whoever violates this alliance shall fall from life and perish with his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever breaks this oath shall fall from life and perish with his clan.

sentences.zh: 皇天後士，祖宗神明，實鑒斯言。”

translations.literal: Heaven above and Earth below, the spirits of ancestors—truly witness these words.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth, the spirits of our ancestors—bear witness to these words.

sentences.zh: 陟等辭旨慷慨，血淚俱下，三軍感激，莫不隕泣。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others spoke with passionate intent; blood and tears flowed together. The three armies were deeply moved, and none failed to weep as if falling stars.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and the others spoke with burning conviction, blood and tears mingling. The whole army was stirred; every man wept.

sentences.zh: 其後江表樹碑以紀忠烈。

translations.literal: Afterward a stele was erected south of the Yangtze to record their loyal valor.
translations.idiomatic: Later the region south of the Yangtze raised a stele to commemorate their loyal valor.

sentences.zh: 無何，有詔令陟赴行在。

translations.literal: Before long there was an edict ordering Zhi to proceed to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict ordered Zhi to proceed to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 陟以廣琛雖承恩命，猶且遲回，恐後變生，禍貽於陟，欲往招慰，然後赴征，乃發使上表，懇言其急。

translations.literal: Zhi thought that although Guangchen had received the gracious appointment, he still hesitated, fearing that later trouble would arise and disaster would reach Zhi. He wished to go first to win him over and then answer the summons, so he sent a messenger with a memorial urgently stating the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi feared that although Guangchen had received imperial favor he still wavered, and that delay might bring disaster upon himself. He wished to reassure Guangchen before answering the summons, and sent an urgent memorial to that effect.

sentences.zh: 陟馳至曆陽，見廣琛，且宣恩旨，勞徠行賞，陟自以私馬數匹賜之，安其疑懼。

translations.literal: Zhi galloped to Liyang, saw Guangchen, announced the gracious intent, comforted and rewarded him, and personally gave him several of his own horses to settle his doubts and fears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi rode hard to Liyang, met Guangchen, announced the imperial message, offered comfort and rewards, and gave him several of his own horses to ease his fears.

sentences.zh: 即日便赴行在，謁見肅宗，肅宗深器之，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: That same day he proceeded to the imperial camp, had an audience with Suzong, and Suzong greatly valued him and appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he reached the emperor's camp and was received by Suzong, who held him in high regard and appointed him censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 拾遺杜甫上表論房琯有大臣度，真宰相器，聖朝不容，辭旨迂誕，肅宗令崔光遠與陟及憲部尚書顏真卿同訊之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Du Fu submitted a memorial arguing that Fang Guan had the measure of a great minister and was truly material for a chief minister, yet the sage court would not tolerate him. The wording was roundabout and extravagant. Suzong ordered Cui Guangyuan, together with Zhi and Minister of Justice Yan Zhenqing, to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Du Fu memorialized that Fang Guan had the stature of a great minister and the makings of a true chancellor, yet the court would not keep him. The language was extravagant and far-fetched. Suzong ordered Cui Guangyuan, Zhi, and Minister of Justice Yan Zhenqing to investigate.

sentences.zh: 陟因入奏曰：“杜甫所論房琯事，雖被貶黜，不失諫臣大體。”

translations.literal: Zhi then entered and memorialized, saying: "Du Fu's discussion of the Fang Guan affair, though Fang was demoted and dismissed, did not depart from the great principle of a remonstrating minister."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi entered and reported: "Du Fu's defense of Fang Guan, though Fang was demoted, still upheld the proper role of a remonstrating minister."

sentences.zh: 上由此疏之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby came to be distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense and grew distant from him.

sentences.zh: 時朝臣立班多不整肅，至有班頭相吊哭者，乃罷陟御史大夫，顏真卿代，授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the time when court ministers stood in formation many were not properly disciplined, to the point that the heads of ranks wept and mourned for each other. Thereupon Zhi was removed as Censor-in-Chief, Yan Zhenqing replaced him, and Zhi was given the post of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Court formations had grown so disorderly that men at the head of the ranks were seen weeping over one another. Zhi was removed as censor-in-chief—Yan Zhenqing took his place—and appointed minister of personnel instead.

sentences.zh: 自後任事寵臣，皆後來初用，望風畏忌，道竟不行。

translations.literal: From then on the favored ministers who held office were all newly appointed latecomers. They feared him at sight and kept their distance, and his path was ultimately blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the favored ministers then in power were all recent appointees who feared and avoided him, and his reforms never took hold.

sentences.zh: 因宗人伐墓柏，坐不能禁，出為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Because clansmen cut down cypress trees at a tomb and he was unable to stop them, he was sent out as Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen felled cypresses at a family tomb and he failed to stop them, he was sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，入為太常卿。

translations.literal: In Qianyuan 2 he entered the capital as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 2 he returned to the capital as minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 呂諲再入相，薦為禮部尚書、東京留守，判尚書省事，兼東京畿觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: When Lü Yin again entered the chancellorship he recommended Zhi as Minister of Rites, Eastern Capital Intendant, with charge of the Secretariat affairs, and also Commissioner for Observation and Disposition in the Eastern Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yin returned to the chancellorship he recommended Zhi as minister of rites and intendant of the eastern capital, with charge of secretariat affairs and oversight of the eastern capital region.

sentences.zh: 逆賊史思明寇逼河洛，副元帥李光弼議守河陽，令陟率東京官屬入關回避，乃令兵守陝州。

translations.literal: The rebel Shi Siming pressed upon the He-Luo region. Vice Commander Li Guangbi planned to hold Heyang and ordered Zhi to lead the eastern capital officials into the passes to withdraw, then ordered troops to hold Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Shi Siming threatened the He-Luo region, vice commander Li Guangbi planned to hold Heyang and ordered Zhi to lead eastern capital officials into the passes for safety while troops guarded Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 有詔遷吏部尚書，留守如故，令止於永樂，不許至京，候光弼收復河洛，令陟依前居守。

translations.literal: There was an edict transferring him to Minister of Personnel while he remained intendant as before, ordering him to stop at Yongle and not permitted to reach the capital, to wait until Guangbi recovered the He-Luo region, then ordered Zhi to resume his former guard duties.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to minister of personnel while keeping him as intendant, but ordered him to remain at Yongle and not enter the capital until Guangbi had recovered the He-Luo region, when he was to resume his former duties.

sentences.zh: 陟早有台輔之望，間被李林甫、楊國忠所擠。

translations.literal: Zhi had long been expected for a top post at court, but was repeatedly squeezed out by Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had long been expected for the highest offices, but was repeatedly pushed aside by Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 及中原兵起，天下事殷，陟常自謂負經緯之器，遭後生騰謗，明主見疑，常鬱鬱不得誌，乃歎曰：“吾道窮於此乎，有誌不伸，得非天命乎！”

translations.literal: When warfare rose in the Central Plains and affairs under Heaven grew urgent, Zhi often considered himself possessed of the talent to govern the realm, yet suffered slander from younger men and suspicion from a clear-sighted ruler. He was often depressed and unable to fulfill his ambition, and sighed, saying: "Has my path ended here? Ambition unfulfilled—is this not Heaven's decree!"
translations.idiomatic: When war engulfed the heartland and the empire's troubles multiplied, Zhi felt himself born to govern yet was slandered by juniors and mistrusted by his sovereign. Depressed and unable to act, he sighed: "Has my road ended here? Ambition thwarted—is this not fate?"

sentences.zh: 因遘疾，上元元年八月，卒於虢州，時年六十五，贈荊州大都督。

translations.literal: He then fell ill. In the eighth month of Shangyuan 1 he died at Guozhou, aged sixty-five, and was posthumously given the title of Grand General of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died at Guozhou in the eighth month of Shangyuan 1, aged sixty-five. He was posthumously made grand general of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，詔曰：“竭忠之臣，歿不廢命，奉上之節，行固無私，言念飾終，抑惟恒典。

translations.literal: In Yongtai 1 an edict said: "A minister who exhausts his loyalty, though dead does not abandon his charge; the integrity of serving above is in conduct without selfishness. Speaking of honoring the end—this is the constant rule."
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1 an edict declared: "A loyal minister, though dead, does not abandon his charge; service to the throne brooks no selfishness. To honor him at life's end is the constant way."

sentences.zh: 故金紫光祿大夫、吏部尚書、兼御史大夫、充東京留守、兼判留司尚書省事、東京畿觀察處置使、上柱國、郇國公韋陟，敦敏直方，端嚴峻整，弘敷典禮，表正人倫，學冠通儒，文含大雅。

translations.literal: The late Jinzi Guanglu Daifu, Minister of Personnel, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Eastern Capital Intendant, with charge of the Remaining Secretariat affairs, Commissioner for Observation and Disposition in the Eastern Capital Region, Shangzhuguo, Duke of Xun Wei Zhi—diligent, perceptive, upright, and square; dignified, stern, and orderly; broadly spreading canonical rites and setting right human relations; learning surpassing the comprehensive ru; writing containing the great elegance.
translations.idiomatic: The late Jinzi Guanglu Daifu, Minister of Personnel, concurrent censor-in-chief, intendant of the eastern capital with charge of remaining secretariat affairs, commissioner for the eastern capital region, Shangzhuguo, Duke of Xun Wei Zhi—was diligent and perceptive, upright and stern, a champion of ritual and moral order, a scholar among scholars, a writer of the highest elegance.

sentences.zh: 頃者詢謨舊德，保厘成周，眷彼郊圻，資其慎固。

translations.literal: Recently, as an old worthy in counsel, he preserved and regulated the eastern capital; cherishing that capital region, he was entrusted with its careful defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, as a veteran counselor, he had guarded and governed the eastern capital; the realm relied on his steadfast defense of that critical region.

sentences.zh: 而凶胡殘醜，密邇河洛，命居陝、虢，時俟翦除。

translations.literal: Yet the vicious barbarian remnant pressed close upon the He-Luo region. He was ordered to reside at Shaan and Guo, awaiting the time to cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebel barbarians pressed close on He-Luo. He was posted to Shaan and Guo, awaiting the day they would be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 才加喉舌之榮，遽嬰霜露之疾。

translations.literal: He had just received the glory of the imperial voice when he suddenly fell prey to illness of frost and dew.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely received the honor of a court voice when he was suddenly stricken with mortal illness.

sentences.zh: 方期克享眉壽，冀其有瘳，奄此殂歿，良深震悼。

translations.literal: Just when we expected him to enjoy long life and hoped for his recovery, suddenly came this death—deeply shocking and mournful.
translations.idiomatic: We had looked for him to live out a long span and hoped for his recovery; his sudden death fills us with shock and grief.

sentences.zh: 升車而復，以申三禭之恩；

translations.literal: To raise the carriage and return him is to extend the grace of the three shrouds;
translations.idiomatic: Let the carriage be raised to return him, extending the grace of the three funeral shrouds;

sentences.zh: 在牖加紳，宜崇八座之寵。

translations.literal: To add the sash at the window is to honor the favor due the Eight Seats.
translations.idiomatic: and let the sash be added at the window, honoring the dignity owed a minister of the Eight Seats.

sentences.zh: 可贈尚書左僕射。”

translations.literal: He may be posthumously given the title of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太常博士程皓議諡為“忠孝”。

translations.literal: Taichang Doctor Cheng Hao proposed the posthumous title "Loyal and Filial."
translations.idiomatic: Court ritualist Cheng Hao proposed the posthumous name "Loyal and Filial."

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書顏真卿以為忠則以身許國，見危致命，孝則晨昏色養，取樂庭闈，不合二行殊難，以成 “忠孝”。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Yan Zhenqing held that loyalty means devoting one's body to the state and facing peril to give one's life, while filial piety means attending morning and evening with proper demeanor and finding joy in the family courtyard—the two virtues do not fit together, and it is hard to combine them into "Loyal and Filial."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of justice Yan Zhenqing argued that loyalty means giving one's life for the state in peril, while filial piety means daily care for parents at home—the two virtues are distinct and cannot easily be fused into "Loyal and Filial."

sentences.zh: 主客員外郎歸崇敬又駁之，紛議不已。

translations.literal: Principal Secretary of the Bureau of Receptions Gui Chongjing again refuted it, and contentious debate continued without end.
translations.idiomatic: Principal secretary of the bureau of receptions Gui Chongjing objected as well, and debate raged on.

sentences.zh: 右僕射郭英乂不達其體，請從太常之狀而奏。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Guo Yingyi did not grasp the principle and requested to follow the Taichang submission and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Right vice director Guo Yingyi missed the point and asked that the court ritualists' proposal be adopted.

sentences.zh: 陟子允。

translations.literal: Zhi's son was Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son was Yun.

sentences.zh: 斌，景雲初安石為宰輔時，授太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: Bin, when at the beginning of Jingyun Anshi was chief minister, was appointed Crown Prince's Director of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, when Anshi became chief minister at the start of the Jingyun era, was appointed director of communications to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 早修整，尚文藝，容止嚴厲，有大臣體，與兄陟齊名。

translations.literal: Early he was well groomed, valued literary arts, his bearing stern and imposing, with the deportment of a great minister. He was equally famous with his elder brother Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was polished and cultivated, devoted to letters, stern and imposing in bearing, with the deportment of a great minister. He was as renowned as his elder brother Zhi.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，司徒薛王業為女平恩縣主求婚，以斌才地奏配焉。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 17, Situ Prince of Xue Ye sought a marriage for his daughter the Princess of Ping'en. Because of Bin's talent and pedigree he memorialized to match her with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 17, Situ Prince Ye of Xue sought a husband for his daughter, Princess Ping'en, and because of Bin's talent and pedigree memorialized to match them in marriage.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretary assistant.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，轉國子司業，徐安貞、王維、崔顥，當代辭人，特為推挹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he became Vice Director of the Directorate of Education. Xu Anzhen, Wang Wei, and Cui Hao, literary men of the age, especially praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he became vice director of the directorate of education. Xu Anzhen, Wang Wei, and Cui Hao, the leading writers of the day, singled him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，拜中書舍人，兼集賢院學士。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he was appointed Zhongshu Sheren and also Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he was made a drafting official and also an academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 兄陟先為中書舍人，未幾遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhi had first been Zhongshu Sheren; before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhi had first served as drafting official and soon rose to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 陟在南省，斌又掌文誥。

translations.literal: Zhi was in the Southern Secretariat; Bin again handled imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi served in the southern secretariat; Bin again held charge of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 改太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，右相李林甫構陷刑部尚書韋堅，斌以親累貶巴陵太守，移臨安太守，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao, Chancellor of the Right Li Linfu framed Minister of Justice Wei Jian. Bin was demoted to Prefect of Baling because of kin association, then moved to Prefect of Lin'an and given the rank of Yinqing Guanglu Daifu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 5, Chancellor of the Right Li Linfu framed Minister of Justice Wei Jian. Bin was demoted to prefect of Baling through kin association, then transferred to prefect of Lin'an with the rank of Yinqing Guanglu Daifu.

sentences.zh: 斌授五品時，兄陟為河東太守，堂兄由為右金吾將軍，縚為太子少師，四人同時列戟，衣冠之盛，罕有其比。

translations.literal: When Bin received fifth rank, his elder brother Zhi was Prefect of Hedong, his elder cousin You was General of the Right Jinwu Guard, and cousin Tao was Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince. The four at the same time displayed halberds at their gates—the splendor of office and dress rarely had its equal.
translations.idiomatic: When Bin received fifth rank, his brother Zhi was prefect of Hedong, his elder cousin You was general of the right Jinwu Guard, and cousin Tao was junior tutor of the crown prince. All four bore halberds at their gates at once—a display of rank rarely matched.

sentences.zh: 十四載，安祿山反，陷洛陽，斌為賊所得，偽授黃門侍郎，憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year An Lushan rebelled and took Luoyang. Bin was captured by the rebels, falsely appointed Vice Director of the Palace Gate, and died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year An Lushan rebelled and took Luoyang. Bin fell into rebel hands, was given the false title of vice director of the palace gate, and died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 及克復兩京，肅宗乾元元年，贈秘書監。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, in Qianyuan 1 of Suzong he was posthumously given the title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, Suzong in Qianyuan 1 posthumously made him director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安石兄叔夏別有傳。

translations.literal: Anshi's elder brother Shuxia has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's elder brother Shuxia has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 從父兄子抗，從祖兄子巨源。

translations.literal: His paternal cousin's son was Kang; his father's elder cousin's son was Juyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin's son was Kang; his father's elder cousin's son was Juyuan.

sentences.zh: 抗，弱冠舉明經，累轉吏部郎中，以清謹著稱。

translations.literal: Kang, in his early twenties passed the Mingjing examination, rose through several posts to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and was known for purity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Kang passed the Mingjing examination in his early twenties, rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel, and was known for purity and prudence.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，為永昌令，不務威刑而政令肅一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun he was Magistrate of Yongchang. He did not rely on harsh punishments yet government orders were uniformly strict.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingyun he was magistrate of Yongchang. Without harsh punishments he kept government uniformly strict.

sentences.zh: 都輦繁劇，前後為政，寬猛得中，無如抗者。

translations.literal: The capital region was complex and demanding. Among those who governed before and after, none balanced lenience and severity as well as Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The capital district was complex and demanding. Of all who governed it before and after, none matched Kang in balancing lenience and severity.

sentences.zh: 無幾，遷右台御史中丞，人吏詣闕請留，不許，因立碑於通衢，紀其遺惠。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right Office. Officials and commoners went to the palace to request he be kept, but this was not permitted; therefore a stele was erected at the thoroughfare to record his lingering beneficence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the right office. Officials and commoners petitioned the throne to keep him, but in vain; they raised a stele at the crossroads to record his legacy of good rule.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，自左庶子出為益州長史。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 3 he went out from Left Subordinate Director to Long Administrator of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 3 he left the post of left subordinate director to become long administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered the capital as Vice Director of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to the capital as vice director of the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 八年，河曲叛胡康待賓擁徒作亂，詔抗持節慰撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the rebellious Hu Kang Daibin of the Hequ region gathered followers and raised disorder. An edict ordered Kang to go with full credentials to comfort and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the rebel Hu Kang Daibin of the Hequ region gathered followers and rose in revolt. Kang was ordered to proceed with full credentials to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 抗素無武略，不為寇所憚。

translations.literal: Kang had never had military skill and was not feared by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Kang had no military experience and the bandits did not fear him.

sentences.zh: 在路遲留不敢進，因墜馬稱疾，竟不至賊所而還。

translations.literal: On the road he delayed and dared not advance, then fell from his horse and claimed illness, and in the end never reached the bandits' place but returned.
translations.idiomatic: He lingered on the road and dared not advance, then fell from his horse and pleaded illness, and never reached the rebels at all.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官檢校鴻臚卿，代王晙為御史大夫，兼按察京畿。

translations.literal: Soon, with his original rank he was made Acting Director of the Office of the Imperial Stud and replaced Wang Jun as Censor-in-Chief, also Investigating Commissioner for the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, retaining his original rank, he was made acting director of the office of the imperial stud and replaced Wang Jun as censor-in-chief, with additional charge of investigating the capital region.

sentences.zh: 時抗弟拯為萬年令，兄弟同領本部，時人榮之。

translations.literal: At the time Kang's younger brother Zheng was Magistrate of Wannian. The brothers together headed the same region, and people of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his younger brother Zheng was magistrate of Wannian. The two brothers together governed the same region—a distinction the age admired.

sentences.zh: 尋以薦御史非其人，出為安州都督，轉蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, because he recommended a censor who was not the right man, he was sent out as Military Commissioner of Anzhou and transferred to Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because he had recommended an unworthy man as censor, he was sent out as military commissioner of Anzhou and then transferred to prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，入為大理卿，其年代陸象先為刑部尚書，尋又分掌吏部選事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review. In that year he replaced Lu Xiangxian as Minister of Justice, and soon also shared charge of selection affairs in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became director of the court of judicial review. That year he replaced Lu Xiangxian as minister of justice, and soon also shared charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 抗曆職以清儉自守，不務產業，及終，喪事殆不能給。

translations.literal: Kang through his offices kept himself pure and frugal and did not pursue estates. When he died the funeral could scarcely be provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Kang served with purity and frugality and never built up estates. At his death his family could barely afford the funeral.

sentences.zh: 玄宗聞其貧，特令給靈輿，遞送還鄉。

translations.literal: Xuanzong heard of his poverty and specially ordered a funeral carriage provided and relay transport to send him home.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong learned of his poverty and specially ordered a funeral carriage and relay transport to send him home.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少傅，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, with posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior tutor of the crown prince, with the posthumous name Zhen ("Upright").

sentences.zh: 抗為京畿按察使時，舉奉天尉梁升卿、新豐尉王倕、金城尉王冰、華原尉王燾為判官及度支使，其後升卿等皆名位通顯，時人以抗有知人之鑒。

translations.literal: When Kang was Investigating Commissioner for the Capital Region he recommended Fengtian District Assistant Liang Shengqing, Xinfeng District Assistant Wang Wei, Jincheng District Assistant Wang Bing, and Huayuan District Assistant Wang Tao as judges and fiscal commissioners. Later Shengqing and the others all reached prominent rank and fame, and people of the time considered Kang to have the discernment to know men.
translations.idiomatic: As investigating commissioner for the capital region Kang recommended Liang Shengqing of Fengtian, Wang Wei of Xinfeng, Wang Bing of Jincheng, and Wang Tao of Huayuan as judges and fiscal commissioners. All later rose to prominence, and the age credited Kang with a discerning eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 巨源，周京兆尹總曾孫也。

translations.literal: Juyuan was the great-grandson of Zhou's Governor of Jingzhao, Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan was the great-grandson of Zong, governor of Jingzhao under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖匡伯，襲祖爵鄖國公，入隋改封舒國公，官至尚衣奉禦。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuangbo inherited his grandfather's title Duke of Yun, entered Sui and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Shu, and reached the office of Director of Imperial Wardrobe Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuangbo inherited the title Duke of Yun, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shu under Sui, and rose to director of imperial wardrobe attendants.

sentences.zh: 巨源則天時累遷司賓少卿，轉司府卿、文昌右丞、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's time Juyuan rose through several posts to Vice Director of the Bureau of Guest Affairs, then Director of the Treasury, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Concurrent Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Juyuan rose to vice director of the bureau of guest affairs, then director of the treasury, right vice director of the secretariat, and concurrent associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.

sentences.zh: 三年，轉夏官侍郎，依前平章事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Vice Minister of War, continuing as before as Associate Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to vice minister of war while continuing as associate director.

sentences.zh: 有吏才，勾覆省內文案，下符剝徵，雖為下所怨苦，然亦頗收其利。

translations.literal: He had administrative talent, audited documents within the secretariat, issued orders and collected levies. Though the subordinates resented and suffered, he also quite reaped profit.
translations.idiomatic: He had administrative talent and audited secretariat documents, issuing orders and pressing collections. Though subordinates resented him, the treasury profited.

sentences.zh: 證聖初，出為鄜州刺史，尋拜地官尚書、神都留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhensheng he was sent out as Prefect of Fu and soon appointed Minister of Earthly Affairs and Intendant of Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhensheng he was sent out as prefect of Fu, then appointed minister of earthly affairs and intendant of the divine capital.

sentences.zh: 長安二年，詔入轉刑部尚書，又加太子賓客，再為神都留守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an an edict summoned him to transfer to Minister of Justice, also given the additional post of Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince, and again made Intendant of Shendu.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an 2 he was recalled to minister of justice, also made senior mentor to the crown prince, and again intendant of the divine capital.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，入拜工部尚書，封同安縣子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he entered as Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Tong'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong he entered as minister of works and was enfeoffed as viscount of Tong'an.

sentences.zh: 又遷吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，進封郇縣伯。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of Personnel and Concurrent Third Rank under the Secretariat and Chancellery, and advanced to Earl of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to minister of personnel and third rank under the secretariat and chancellery, and advanced to earl of Xun.

sentences.zh: 時安石為中書令，以是巨源近屬，罷知政事。

translations.literal: At the time Anshi was Zhongshu Ling; because Juyuan was a close kinsman, he was removed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Anshi was chief minister; because Juyuan was a close kinsman, he was removed from managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 巨源尋遷侍中、中書令，進封舒國公，附入韋後三等親，敘為兄弟，編在屬籍。

translations.literal: Juyuan soon moved to Palace Attendant and Zhongshu Ling, advanced to Duke of Shu, attached himself to Empress Wei's third-rank kin, was reckoned as brothers, and entered in the imperial genealogy.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan soon became palace attendant and chief minister, was advanced to duke of Shu, attached himself to Empress Wei's third-rank kin, was reckoned as her brother, and entered the imperial genealogy.

sentences.zh: 是歲，巨源奉制與唐休璟、李懷遠、祝欽明、蘇環等定《垂拱格》及《格後敕》，前後計二十卷，頒下施行。

translations.literal: That year Juyuan received orders together with Tang Xiujing, Li Huaiyuan, Zhu Qinming, and Su Huan to compile the Chui Gong Code and Post-Code Edicts, twenty volumes in all, which were promulgated and put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: That year Juyuan was ordered with Tang Xiujing, Li Huaiyuan, Zhu Qinming, and Su Huan to compile the Chui Gong Code and Post-Code Edicts—twenty volumes in all—which were promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 時武三思先有實封數千戶在貝州，時屬大水，刺史宋璟議稱租庸及封丁並合捐免；

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sansi already had a substantive fief of several thousand households in Beizhou. It happened to be a great flood. Prefect Song Jing proposed that land tax, corvée, and fief households all ought to be remitted;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi already held a substantive fief of several thousand households in Beizhou when a great flood struck. Prefect Song Jing proposed that land tax, corvée, and fief obligations all be remitted;

sentences.zh: 巨源以為穀稼雖被湮沉，其蠶桑見在，可勒輸庸調，由是河朔戶口頗多流散。

translations.literal: Juyuan held that although grain crops had been submerged, the mulberry and silkworm fields still existed and corvée and tax could be compelled. Because of this the population north of the Yellow River largely scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan argued that though grain fields were flooded, mulberry and silkworm crops remained and corvée and tax could still be collected. The population north of the Yellow River largely fled as a result.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，順天翊聖皇后衣箱中裙上有五色雲起，久則方歇，巨源以為非常佳瑞，請布告天下，許之。

translations.literal: In Jinglong 2, on the skirt in Empress Shuntian Yisheng's clothes chest five-colored clouds arose and after a long time only then subsided. Juyuan considered this an extraordinary excellent omen and requested it be proclaimed to all under Heaven. This was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 2 five-colored clouds appeared on a skirt in Empress Shuntian Yisheng's wardrobe and lingered long before fading. Juyuan hailed this as a marvelous omen and asked that it be proclaimed to the realm. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 中宗又令畫工圖其狀以示百僚，仍大赦天下，內外五品已上官母妻各加封邑。

translations.literal: Zhongzong also ordered painters to depict its form to show the hundred officials, still granted a great amnesty to all under Heaven, and added fief to the mothers and wives of officials inside and outside of fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong had painters depict the phenomenon for the court, proclaimed a general amnesty, and added fiefs to the mothers and wives of officials of fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 時中宗即雅信符瑞，巨源又讚成其妖妄。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongzong already greatly trusted portents and omens, and Juyuan again praised and completed his delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong already doted on portents and omens, and Juyuan egged on his delusions.

sentences.zh: 是歲星墜如雷，野雉皆雊，咎征若此，不聞巨源有言，蓋與韋皇后繼敘源流，佞媚官爵，疑其開導，以踵則天。

translations.literal: That year stars fell like thunder and wild pheasants all crowed—omens of disaster like this. One did not hear Juyuan speak. Likely because he had continued kinship with Empress Wei, fawned for office and rank, and was suspected of opening the way to follow Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: That same year stars fell like thunder and wild pheasants crowed everywhere—clear omens of disaster—yet Juyuan said nothing. Having tied himself to Empress Wei for rank and favor, he was suspected of paving the way to revive Wu Zetian's path.

sentences.zh: 時有驍衛將軍迦葉誌忠、太常少卿鄭愔、兵部尚書宗楚客、右補闕趙延禧等，或相諷諭，或上表章，謬說符祥，朋黨取媚，識者嗟憤。

translations.literal: At the time there were General of the Brave Guard Ye Zhizhong, Vice Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yin, Minister of War Zong Chuke, and Remonstrance Official Zhao Yanxi and others, some offering indirect admonition, some submitting memorials, all falsely speaking of auspicious signs, forming factions to gain favor. Knowing men sighed and were indignant.
translations.idiomatic: General Ye Zhizhong of the brave guard, vice minister of ceremonies Zheng Yin, minister of war Zong Chuke, remonstrance official Zhao Yanxi, and others either offered veiled flattery or submitted memorials falsely praising omens, forming factions to curry favor. Thoughtful men sighed in anger.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，拜尚書左僕射，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In Jinglong 3 he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, continuing as before in managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 3 he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs while continuing to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又拜尚書令、同中書門下三品，仍舊監修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Third Rank under the Secretariat and Chancellery, still continuing to supervise compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made director of the Department of State Affairs and third rank under the secretariat and chancellery, still supervising compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 時國家將有事於南郊，而巨源希韋後之旨，協同祝欽明之議，言皇后合助郊祀，竟以皇后為亞獻，巨源為終獻，又以大臣女為齋娘。

translations.literal: At the time the state was about to perform the southern suburban sacrifice, and Juyuan hoped to please Empress Wei's intent. He agreed with Zhu Qinming's proposal, saying the empress ought to assist in the suburban sacrifice. In the end the empress was made secondary offerer, Juyuan the final offerer, and daughters of great ministers were made fasting maidens.
translations.idiomatic: When the state prepared the southern suburban sacrifice, Juyuan sought to please Empress Wei. Agreeing with Zhu Qinming, he argued the empress should assist at the rite. The empress became secondary offerer, Juyuan the final offerer, and ministers' daughters were made fasting maidens.

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人之難，家人令巨源逃匿，巨源曰：“吾國之大臣，豈得聞難不赴？”

translations.literal: When the disaster of Empress Wei occurred, family members told Juyuan to flee and hide. Juyuan said: "I am a great minister of the state—how can I hear of disaster and not go?"
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei's coup collapsed, his family urged him to flee. Juyuan said, "I am a great minister of the state—how can I hear of trouble and not go?"

sentences.zh: 乃出，至都街，為亂兵所殺，時年八十。

translations.literal: He then went out, reached the capital street, and was killed by mutinous soldiers, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He went out into the capital street and was killed by mutinous soldiers, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 夫古之諡，在乎勸沮，將杜小人之業，冀長君子之風。

translations.literal: Ancient posthumous names lay in encouragement and deterrence, intending to block the pursuits of petty men and hoping to lengthen the wind of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient posthumous names were meant to encourage virtue and deter vice—to block petty men's pursuits and nurture gentlemen's conduct.

sentences.zh: 故為善者雖存不貴仕，而沒有餘名，此賢達所以砥節也；

translations.literal: Therefore those who did good, though living did not seek high office, yet in death left a surplus of name—this is why the worthy and accomplished honed their integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Those who did good, though they did not crave office in life, left honorable names in death—thus the worthy tempered their character;

sentences.zh: 為惡者雖生有所幸，死懷所懲，此回邪所以易心也。

translations.literal: those who did evil, though living had their luck, in death harbored what they feared as punishment—this is why the crooked and perverse changed their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: those who did evil, though lucky in life, feared punishment in death—thus the crooked were moved to change.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 巨源嚐未斯察，而乃聞義不從，與惡相濟，蓄罔上之誌，協群凶之謀，苟容聖朝，貪昧厚祿。

translations.literal: Juyuan never once examined this, yet heard of righteousness and did not follow, aided evil, harbored intent to deceive above, and joined the plots of the wicked gang, tolerating the sage court while greedily enjoying thick salary.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan never grasped this. He heard righteousness and turned away, abetted evil, nursed treasonous intent, and joined the wicked in their plots—clinging to office while gorging on emolument.

sentences.zh: 自以宰臣之貴，不崇朝而賈害者，固鬼得而誅之也。

translations.literal: He considered himself precious as a chief minister, yet before one morning had passed suffered harm—truly ghosts could execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He deemed himself precious as a chief minister, yet within a morning met his doom—as if ghosts themselves had executed him.

sentences.zh: 彼則匹夫之微，未受命而行刑者，固人得而誅之也。

translations.literal: Those were but the slightness of common men, executing punishment without receiving mandate—truly men could execute them.
translations.idiomatic: They were but common men, meting out punishment without mandate—yet men could justly slay them.

sentences.zh: 幽明之憤，斷焉可知，天地之心，自此而見矣。

translations.literal: The indignation of the hidden and manifest is clearly knowable; the heart of Heaven and Earth is thereby seen.
translations.idiomatic: The wrath of the seen and unseen worlds is plain to see; the mind of Heaven and Earth stands revealed.

sentences.zh: 頃者皇運中興，功臣翼政。

translations.literal: Recently the imperial fortune was restored, and meritorious ministers assisted government.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the dynasty was restored and meritorious ministers helped govern.

sentences.zh: 時序未幾，邪逆執權，奸慝者拜爵於私門，忠正者黜降於藩郡。

translations.literal: Before long the sequence of time had hardly passed when the wicked and rebellious seized power. The treacherous and vicious received titles at private gates; the loyal and upright were demoted to frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had time passed when the wicked seized power. Traitors were ennobled at private gates; the loyal were banished to frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 巨源此際，用事方殷。

translations.literal: At this juncture Juyuan's power was at its height.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Juyuan's power was at its height.

sentences.zh: 且於阿韋何親，而結為昆季；

translations.literal: Moreover, what kin was he to the Wei clan that he was joined as sworn brothers?
